title: Alien Life Can Survive on This Tiny Moon—We Just Need to Go Find It
content:
Welcome back to the Abstract! Here are the studies this week that sailed alien seas, beat the heat, went retro, and got caught in the food web.

First, scientists make the case that Saturn’s moon Enceladus could resolve one of humanity’s greatest questions—are we alone in the universe?—if only we would just send a spacecraft there already. Then: an amoeba in hot water, a backwards-ass planet, and the prandial ouroboros we call life on Earth.

As always, for more of my work, check out my book First Contact: The Story of Our Obsession with Aliens, or subscribe to my personal newsletter the BeX Files. 

Helmbrecht, Vanessa et al. “Enceladus-like geochemistry fuels methanogenesis under extreme CO2 limitation.” Science Advances.

Postberg, Frank, Zou, Zenghui et al. “Cassini CDA observes compositional segregation of Enceladus’ ice grains from slow freezing and fragmentation of oceanic spray.” Science Advances.

In a double-whammy pair of studies, scientists have offered more proof that Enceladus—the tiny moon of Saturn—might host alien life, and that it would be relatively easy to find out for sure.

title: Kun puolustukseen virtaa miljardeja, tällaisia strategisia riskejä jättihankinnoissa piilee
content:
Jos asevoimat ostaa uutta kalustoa nopeammin kuin mitä sitä pystytään vastaanottamaan, käyttämään tai varastoimaan, ollaan vaaran vyöhykkeellä. Kenellä olisi kokonaiskuva Suomen puolustustalouden tarkoituksenmukaisuudesta?

Suomen puolustukseen virtaa rahaa ennennäkemättömällä vauhdilla. Uusia asejärjestelmiä hankitaan ja vanhaa kalustoa päivitetään samalla, kun puolustusmenojen tasoa nostetaan Nato-tavoitteiden mukaisesti.

Vaarana on, että investointien nopea nosto voi johtaa strategisesti huonoihin ratkaisuihin: ostetaan hyvää tavaraa, mutta sen käyttämiseen ei saada riittävästi varoja.

Paraikaa ilmavoimille rakennetaan F-35-järjestelmää aseineen, merivoimille neljää Pohjanmaa-luokan korvettia ja ilmatorjuntaan uutta Daavidin linko -järjestelmää.

Maavoimille Suomi tilasi keväällä 112 K9-panssarihaupitsia lisää, ja lyhyen kantaman ilmatorjuntaa vahvistetaan Saabin RBS 70 NG -järjestelmillä.

Rahalla saa rautaa, mutta heti käytettävissä olevan puolustuskyvyn rakentaminen on sen sijaan vaikeampi tehtävä.

title: An exiled Myanmar journalist’s story: Echoing public’s voice and resilience
content:
An Exile Hub fellow shares their personal experiences and reflections

Originally published on Global Voices

Image from Exile Hub, used with permission.

Exile Hub is one of Global Voices’ partners in Southeast Asia, emerging in response to the 2021 coup in Myanmar, and focusing on empowering journalists and human rights defenders. This article, by Justino, was published on August 12, 2026, and an edited version is republished under a content partnership agreement.

Ever since I was around 10 years old — old enough to begin thinking seriously about the world — I admired journalists. Watching them work, I was fascinated by a profession that seemed so distant from my own life. At the time, journalism was simply something I admired from afar, but one dream stayed with me:

“One day, I want to become a journalist who brings people’s voices to light.”

I carried that dream with me for years.

title: Palestine Gains Recognition While Losing the Land for a State
content:
Diplomatic recognition has widened, but settlement expansion and territorial fragmentation threaten the foundations of Palestinian statehood.

By Ramesh Jaura

BERLIN | NEW YORK | 26 September 2026 (IDN) – Mahmoud Abbas delivered one of the most important speeches of this year’s United Nations General Assembly without being allowed into the hall.

The Palestinian president appeared via recorded video after the United States refused visas to his delegation for the second consecutive year. He called the decision unlawful and contrary to Washington’s responsibilities as host of the United Nations.

His absence added meaning to the speech. The General Assembly is meant to be the one international chamber in which states, large and small, can speak. Yet the representative of a people recognised by most UN members was prevented from appearing because of a decision taken by the host government.

Abbas’s warning went beyond the familiar argument that the two-state solution is in danger. He said Israeli policy threatened the continued existence of Palestinians on the land intended for their state.

title: I Deliberately Bet Like a Problem Gambler. DraftKings Made Me a VIP.
content:
It was late May, the French Open was on and DraftKings was pushing me into the action.

A promotion pinged on my phone. “BET & GET,” it boomed, offering to boost my profits if I threw down on tennis, punctuating the point with a cartoon stack of cash. I was already in the middle of a two-hour betting spree, ripping 64 wagers on the clay courts of Paris from my office chair in New York City.

A $75 bet that Claire Liu would win the fifth point of her first set tiebreak against Maria Sakkari? Wrong. How about an easy $300 on Francisco Comesana to win the first game of the second set against Luciano Darderi? Negativo. 

I’ll be the first to admit that my backhand needs some work. But this wasn’t about sports. It was about scratching an itch.

title: Stripped titles? Compensating rivals? How the Manchester City cheating scandal could play out
content:
One of the biggest cheating scandals in world sports history has erupted in England: Manchester City has reportedly been found guilty of 114 of the 115 alleged breaches of English Premier League financial rules brought against the club in 2023.

The charges relate to the club’s incredibly successful spell between 2009 and 2018 when they won seven major titles, headlined by three Premier League championships.

Manchester City was bought in 2008 by the Abu Dhabi United Group, led by Sheikh Mansour bin Zayed al-Nahyan – a member of the Abu Dhabi royal family.

The group now owns or has a stake in 13 football teams across the world, from New York to Melbourne, meaning there may be ramifications well beyond England.

But Manchester City is expected to appeal, having long protested its innocence – so this case is not over yet.

The guilty findings are a potentially seismic development in a case that has hung over English football for more than three years.

The charges cover several areas, including:

  • the accuracy of financial information supplied to the Premier League
  • player and manager remuneration
  • compliance with Union of European Football Associations (UEFA) and Premier League financial regulations

title: Niger Rejects Key Rights Recommendations at UN Review
content:
Niger has rejected key recommendations raised by United Nations member countries during its Universal Periodic Review (UPR) earlier this year, including calls to address arbitrary detention, discrimination against lesbian, gay, bisexual and transgender (LGBT) people, and accountability for serious human rights violations. 

The UPR is a UN Human Rights Council process in which the human rights records of member states are reviewed by other member countries every five years.

On September 1, Niger’s military junta responded to the 265 recommendations made in May by 97 UN member countries and accepted 254 of them, including commitments to strengthen civilian protection and ensure security forces receive training on international human rights and humanitarian law.

The junta however rejected 11 recommendations addressing some of the country’s most pressing rights concerns, including to reverse its June decision to start the withdrawal process from the International Criminal Court (ICC). Leaving the ICC risks depriving victims of grave international crimes a last resort to seek justice and remedies.

title: Why Museums Matter for Mental Health and Well-Being
content:
Doctors are prescribing gallery visits. Care homes are receiving museum collections. People living with dementia are reliving Eurovision classics with a mobile museum. Here is why museums have become some of the most powerful wellbeing spaces we have.

Most of us who work in museums have felt it. A visitor lingers in front of a painting and leaves looking lighter. A regular at the Tuesday tour turns out to have no one else to talk to all week. A family member tells you their mother, who rarely speaks now, lit up at the sight of an old tin toy.

For a long time, these moments were treated as pleasant side effects. That is changing fast. As health systems strain under rising demand for mental health support, and as loneliness is increasingly recognised as a public health issue in its own right, museums are stepping forward as genuine partners in care.

title: Arvio: Kaksi Sylvia Plathin loistoteosta uusina suomennoksina on kulttuuriteko
content:
Amerikkalaisen kirjailijan Sylvia Plathin (1932-63) on feministinen tutkimus nostanut anglosaksisen kirjallisuuden taivaaseen, eikä syyttä.

Hänen innovoiva kielensä, hänen loistavan kärjekkäät kielikuvansa ovat sen arvoiset.

Mutta eniten hänen maineeseensa on vaikuttanut lyhyt traaginen elämä, mikä päättyi kaasu-uuni-itsemurhaan hänen aviomiehensä, englantilaisen runoilijan Ted Hughesin jätettyä hänet toisen naisen tähden.

Takana oli myös Plathin elinikäinen syvä depressio, minkä takia hän yritti jo varhain itsemurhaa.

VAIKKA molemmat Siltalan julkaisemat Plathin kärkiteokset on käännetty jo aiemmin, uudet suomennokset aiheuttavat ikään kuin kirjailijan jälleensyntymän.

Romaani Lasikello ilmestyi alkukielellä Plathin kuolinvuonna. Se on hyvin omaelämäkerrallinen, mutta tässä tapauksessa se ei haittaa, pikemminkin päin vastoin.

Nuoren Esther Greenwoodin epätoivoiset yritykset pyrkiä menestykseen kirjoittajana ja samalla täyttää amerikkalaisen elämäntavan odotukset menevät pahasti pieleen.

title: Wikimedia Brasil’s Development Best Practices Framework: technical sustainability as an organizational responsibility
content:
In 2025, the Wikidata Query Service went through a split of its graph. The service runs on Blazegraph and had grown past 16 billion triples, adding roughly 1 billion per year. The change was meant to ensure the service’s scalability and stability in the medium term. As an emergency measure to prevent a catastrophic failure, the SPARQL endpoint was split in two: one containing only scholarly articles and another with the rest of Wikidata. The split took effect in May 2025, and queries that need to cross both graphs now require SPARQL federation.

As a result, many queries and tools broke, and many are still not working today. Scholia is the most visible example. The impact was so significant that its maintainers ended up migrating the full graph to a QLever engine, outside Wikimedia infrastructure.

title: Diamond Open Access? | Ubiquity Press
content: From Google's English: Abstract: This article adopts the organizational-theoretical concept of path dependency in open access for analysis. According to this concept, open access publishing is no longer described as a single path, but rather two paths must be fundamentally distinguished, and their relationship to one another analyzed. While the commercial path of open access is now perceived as resistant to transformation, hopes are now pinned on a non-profit path (Diamond Open Access), which is organizationally distinct. The efforts to expand non-commercial publishing infrastructures are a reaction to the transformation agreements with the currently dominant publishing oligopoly. Among the numerous undesirable consequences of these agreements are the continued prevalence of hybrid publishing, the largely absent transformation from the subscription model to gold open access journals, the redistribution of acquisition and publication funds among funding institutions to the benefit of the oligopoly, and thus, overall, a deepening of dependence on publishers. title: What Does Your Data Reveal About Sports Betting Apps? Help ProPublica Find Out.
content:
If you’re one of millions of Americans who have placed an online bet on a sporting event, you know how quickly you can go from celebrating your wins to feeling like the odds are stacked against you.

ProPublica is trying to understand how sports betting apps incentivize users to keep playing and when they warn users to pump the brakes. To do that, we need your help: We’re aiming for at least 250 people to upload their gambling history from apps like FanDuel and DraftKings. We’re not quite there yet, so if you’ve used these apps, you can help our journalists. If you’ve worked in the industry, you can also help us by answering a few questions. (You can also reach us on Signal.) 

Sharing your transaction histories and insights about the apps can help us understand when companies provide boosts, invite you into VIP programs and push responsible gaming notices. Without this data, there is no way to know how the companies truly operate. 

Learn more about this project and how to share your data by visiting our website.

title: In his final UN speech, Macron may have given other leaders a valuable parting gift: the guts to stand up to Trump | Steve Bloomfield
content:
The French president’s resolve seems to have rubbed off on the leaders of other ‘middle powers’

On the first day of the United Nations general assembly this week, two world leaders outlined competing visions for the future. Donald Trump’s speech was disturbingly similar to those he’s given before: a litany of false boasts and odd tangents, peppered with grim military threats against a variety of nation states. Discussing his seven-month war with Iran, he mused over whether to “annihilate the Islamic Republic and do it quickly”.

In Trump’s eyes, the world is there to be ruled – and ruled only by the US, whose economy is “the envy of the world” and military is “the most powerful on Earth”.

Steve Bloomfield is the former international editor of the Observer

title: Museums and Climate: Why Cultural Institutions Belong in the Conversation
content:
From exhibitions that turn industrial heritage into hope to galleries built for climate grief, museums are finding their voice on the defining issue of our time. Here is why they belong at the centre of the conversation.

Climate change is often discussed in the language of data: parts per million, degrees of warming, emissions targets. The numbers matter, but they rarely move people. What moves people is story, place, emotion and community, and those are exactly the things museums do best.

Museums also hold a rare position of public trust. They are places where people of every age and background come to make sense of the world, and they can host difficult conversations without the heat of a political debate. That makes them uniquely placed to help the public understand the climate crisis, cope with how it makes them feel, and believe they can do something about it.

And museums are not just commentators. Their buildings, exhibitions and supply chains carry a real environmental footprint, which gives them the chance to lead by example. Here are four ways museums around the world are proving that cultural institutions belong in the climate conversation.

title: Drones could speed up getting defibrillators to people having cardiac arrests, study suggests
content:
New research suggests the technology could be used to increase out-of-hospital access to life-saving devices

Drones could help cut the time it takes to get a defibrillator to people experiencing cardiac arrests when not in hospital, researchers have suggested.

In the UK alone, there are more than 30,000 out-of-hospital cardiac arrests a year where emergency medical services attempt to resuscitate the individual, according to the British Heart Foundation. However, fewer than one in 10 people survive such an event, and some who do are left with neurological problems.

title: AI Love Song for Mistress Played at Murder Trial Is Most Excruciating Watch in Recent Memory
content:
We debated for a long time about whether to write about the following video, which comes from a murder trial in which a man named Caleb Flynn is accused of killing his wife. The crime is very serious, and very sad, and yet the following video demonstrates something about where we are as a society. 

The trial has received national attention and has been streaming live. Toward the end of the proceedings Thursday, the prosecution played two versions of an AI love song that Flynn, a former American Idol contestant, generated for his mistress. Investigators found the AI song files as well as lyrics for the song in Flynn’s Notes app after using the forensic tool GrayKey to break into his phone. 

“We found audio files on Caleb’s iPhone that seem to have been AI generated and related to his relationship with [his mistress],” Joseph Wilhelm, a forensic investigator testified. “They’re in two different keys. One’s like a happy or upbeat sad song if that makes any sense, and one’s a sad, sad song. I think one’s in a minor key, one’s in a major key, but I’m not a music professional.” 

“Permission to publish, your honor?,” the prosecutor says. 

“You may,” the judge says.

title: El Salvador: Authorities remain silent over request for humanitarian visit to Ruth López
content:
As human rights defender Ruth López spends her second birthday behind bars, Amnesty International reiterates its request to the Salvadoran authorities to conduct a humanitarian visit and calls for her immediate and unconditional release.

On 1 August 2026, Amnesty International sent formal communications to the Attorney General, the Minister of Justice and Public Security, the Director General of Prisons, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and the judge in charge of the case, requesting authorization for a high-level delegation from the organization to visit Ruth López and directly assess her conditions of detention. The request was reiterated on 26 August and, to date, none of the five authorities has responded. Ana Piquer, Amnesty International’s Americas Director, said:

The authorities’ silence appears increasingly deliberate with each passing day. Every minute that passes makes it even more necessary to allow an independent assessment of Ruth’s conditions in prison.”

Ana Piquer, Amnesty International’s Americas Director

title: ‘Concerning’ low sea ice persists as Antarctic hits third-lowest winter peak
content:
Antarctic sea ice has recorded its third-smallest winter peak extent since satellite records began 48 years ago, new data reveals.

Provisional data from the US National Snow and Ice Data Center (NSIDC) shows that Antarctic sea ice hit its annual winter peak on 14 September, with an extent of 17.59m square kilometres (km2).

The organisation notes that the data is still preliminary, adding that “large fluctuations in extent are typical of Antarctic sea ice near the seasonal maximum”.

One expert tells Carbon Brief that it is “concerning to see these low values persisting”, but says that scientists need more time to determine whether this represents a “structural shift” in Antarctic sea ice extent.

Meanwhile, at the Earth’s other pole, Arctic sea ice reached its annual minimum on 12 September, ranking as the joint-10th lowest in the satellite record.

The NSIDC notes that the last 20 years have seen the lowest 20 Arctic sea ice extents in the satellite record.
snippet: Antarctic sea ice has recorded its third-smallest winter peak extent since satellite records began 48 years ago, new data reveals.
creator: Ayesha Tandon

title: How to Fight Putin’s War on Reality
content:
The staggering costs of the war in Ukraine are obvious to the whole world, and Western powers have imposed sanctions to change the Kremlin’s course. Yet Russia’s military aggression continues unabated. Ukraine’s long-range drone strikes have hit deep into Russia’s economic and military core. While this is strategically significant, it is a mistake to assume increased Russian costs will lead to de-escalation.

That assumption rests on a specific model of state behavior: that leaders respond to cost incentives. In an authoritarian system, like Russia’s, the calculus follows a different logic.

Changing an autocrat’s perception of reality is nearly impossible. An authoritarian leader has considerable latitude to interpret reality in ways that serve him, and Vladimir Putin has used it regularly.

The objective of Western policy should therefore not be to change the Russian leader’s worldview; it should be to weaken the regime’s ability to make that worldview credible to Russia’s people.

Modern autocracies do not rely on coercion alone. They also depend on narratives to justify their actions and sustain an image of competence and strength.

title: CDIF DCAT-Syntax Core and Discovery Profiles: Development Plan
content:
CDIF DCAT-Syntax Core and Discovery Profiles: Development Plan: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22942627 

This document is the first in an irregular series of updates on development plans for the Cross-Domain Interoperability Framework (CDIF). It briefly outlines the status and intended process for development of CDIF Core and Discovery profiles based on the W3C DCAT specification, as opposed to Schema.org. While Schema.org was initially chosen as the basis for core CDIF metadata, given its widespread adoption and support in various search engines and other widely used Web-based applications, the need for a similar foundation implemented using DCAT has become apparent, as its adoption is now becoming much broader.

The intention is that a point-for-point correspondence between the two sets of profiles — for DCAT on the one hand and for Schema.org on the other — can be established, and that free converters provided to enable users to produce and consume either flavour as needed. While a single agreed standard is always ideal, it is not in this case a reality, so this approach is seen as necessary.

title: From University Research to Free Knowledge: Academics Discover Wikimedia
content:
Between September 15 and 20, I, Osama Eid (Osps7), had the opportunity to deliver a five-day Wikimedia education program that brought together 10 university academics from three universities to explore how academic expertise and research can contribute to Wikimedia and the wider ecosystem of free knowledge.

The program focused on introducing participants to Wikipedia, Wikidata, and Wikiversity, while creating a foundation for continued academic engagement with Wikimedia projects.

One of the main objectives of the program was to encourage academics to look at Wikipedia from a different perspective, not only as a source of information, but also as a collaborative platform where their published research and expertise can contribute to improving free knowledge.

During the five days of training, participants learned practical approaches to documenting information in Wikipedia, using reliable academic references, and understanding the importance of verification and proper citation.

title: The media has the AI threat all wrong
content:
Note: This article makes reference to a mass shooting. I made a conscious choice not to use the name of the shooter.

For the past several weeks, we’ve been treated to breathless coverage of the supposed major threat presented by artificial intelligence. If we’re to believe the titans of the AI industry and the media reports mindlessly echoing their every utterance, humanity’s years may be numbered.

It’s not because of climate change and how we’re actively making our planet less fit for human habitation. Indeed, many of these prophets of AI doom don’t actually believe climate change is much of a threat at all. It’s also not because increasingly unstable geopolitics is shifting the world toward greater conflict and the risk of global war.

No, the real threat, according to these supposed geniuses, is that in ten years AI could break free from its human developers and decide it wants to kill humanity. If you’re big into science fiction, you might recognize that kind of a narrative: whether HAL 9000 in 2001: A Space Odyssey or The Terminator himself, this notion that our technology will come for us makes for compelling entertainment.

title: Who are Alisher Usmanov and Mikhail Fridman: And why does the EU sanctions decision matter?
content:
The European Union has extended sanctions against more than 3,000 individuals and entities linked to Russia for another three years. At the same time, two Russian billionaires – Alisher Usmanov and Mikhail Fridman – have been removed from the EU sanctions list.

EU member states agreed to extend the restrictive measures until 22 September 2029. The sanctions include travel restrictions, asset freezes and a ban on making funds or other economic resources available to sanctioned individuals and entities. The European Council says the measures are intended to target those responsible for undermining or threatening Ukraine’s territorial integrity, sovereignty and independence.

Until now, the EU’s individual sanctions related to Russia’s war against Ukraine had generally been renewed every six months. This time, member states opted for a significantly longer extension, providing greater predictability about the future of the restrictions.

title: Batteries, Not AI, Will Define the Next Geoeconomic Era: Chinese Dominance and the Western Response
content:
The global transition toward electric vehicles and renewable energy represents a fundamental shift in the world’s techno-economic paradigm. Drawing on discussions during my June 2026 visit to ETLA in Helsinki, this brief argues that the true engine of this transformation is the battery, the foundational technology uniting production and consumption in the emerging electric age. This memorandum is published alongside a companion brief by Petri Rouvinen (2026) examining the EU’s response to this shift, the proposed Industrial Accelerator Act (IAA).

Through decades of deliberate industrial policy, China has secured command over the entire clean technology triad of solar power, batteries, and electric vehicles. Meanwhile, Western automakers, particularly in the United States, risk being stranded on a shrinking island of internal combustion engine technology amid political whiplash.

In this brief, I synthesize the mechanisms driving China’s rise, examine the strategic implications of the electric technology stack, and offer insights for decision-makers seeking to build a competitive and resilient industrial future.

title: Helsinki EPIC Workshop develops three ideas for transnational cooperation on crisis preparedness
content:
On 23 September 2026, the third EPIC workshop brought together members of the NDPHS Occupational Safety and Health Expert Group (OSH EG) and invited experts in Helsinki to continue developing ideas for a future transnational project on workforce resilience and crisis preparedness. The overall workshop concept was developed jointly by the NDPHS Secretariat and Owe Österbacka, Chair of the OSH Expert Group.

The EPIC – “Effectively Prepared in Crisis” project, funded by the Swedish Institute, aims to enhance collaboration on health-related emergency preparedness and crisis response across the NDPHS Partner Countries and Ukraine, while sharing expertise, lessons learned and good practices to strengthen resilience during crises.

title: New video makes the economic case for investing in public interest media to mark World News Day
content:
Disinformation continues to represent a top global threat and with AI further harming access to reliable information while eroding the visibility, and by extension, the viability of quality journalism. As stated by the High Level Panel on Public Interest media a year ago,  it is more urgent than ever to recognise the social and economic value of public interest media and properly invest in it like the public good it is. 

Paris, 25 September 2026. Ahead of World News Day on 28 September, the Forum on Information and Democracy (FID), in partnership with the International Fund for Public Interest Media (IFPIM), has released a short video renewing the call for governments and policymakers to invest in public interest media.

One year ago, the High-Level Panel on Public Interest Media, which was convened by FID and comprising 11 leading economists, including three Nobel Prizes, published a landmark statement making the economic case for such investment. The statement was picked up by over 80 media outlets and helped shape World News Day‘s call to action.

title: Equal rights, unequal choices: making gender equality real for Gen Z
content:
What does gender equality mean if you can work full-time and still not afford to live independently, or if caring for others comes at the cost of your career? For Gen Z, equality cannot be reduced to rights on paper. It must mean having the real freedom and the material means to choose how to live.

Gen Z has grown up with more formal gender equality than any previous generation. Yet the material freedom needed to make that equality real is becoming harder to secure. Young people have more rights, more awareness and more freedom on paper, but increasingly fewer of the material conditions needed to turn that freedom into real choices.

So, what does it mean to be equal? If you cannot afford to leave your parents’ home, if you are forced to leave your region to get a job, if caring for others means giving up your career, or if having children is economically unfeasible, equality on paper starts to look very different in practice. For Gen Z and the generations to come, gender equality must mean more than equal rights: it must mean an equal capacity to exercise those rights and build an independent life.

title: Movement from behind your gadget
content:
Online vs offline protest, how effective it is?

Originally published on Global Voices

Image by Gerd Altmann from Pixabay. Used under a Pixabay license.

This post is part of Global Voices’ September 2026 Spotlight series, “Protest in Democracy.” With this Spotlight, we seek to explore the many forms of protest, the tactics states use to delegitimize and suppress them, and the complex relationship between protest and democracy. You can support this coverage by donating here.

The growing popularity and expanding use of social media have influenced the ways people express themselves. While protests once involved taking to the streets with banners and chants, such activities can now be carried out in the virtual realm. Messages and slogans are now conveyed through hashtags, digital posters, or videos posted across various social media channels. Events such as the Arab Spring and the Occupy Movement have further reinforced the phenomenon of online protest.

Both of them are effective, no?

title: On the Road: Manifesta sheds light on Ruhr heritage
content:
For this episode we’re taking a look at the Manifesta festival and this sixteenth edition of Europe’s nomadic biennial of contemporary art. Running from 21 June to 4 October 2026, it unfolds across the entire Ruhr region, taking in the major industrial centres of Bochum, Duisburg, Essen and Gelsenkirchen.

Presented by John Beauchamp and Katarzyna Jagodzińska. In the podcast we hear from Founding Director of Manifesta Hedwig Fijen, who steps down from her post in October 2026, and veteran Polish curator, historian and art critic Anda Rottenberg.

Under the title “This is not a church,” more than one hundred participating artists and collectives have transformed twelve church buildings into spaces for exhibitions, performances, workshops and community life. Only two remain consecrated, with one turned into a lay chapel. The others are closed, unused, in the process of deconsecration or have already been repurposed.

Can Manifesta arts festival save Ruhr churches?

title: Najmeh Amini Faces Death Sentence and Over 12 Years in Prison Following Arrest During January Protests
content:
According to HRANA, Najmeh Amini is currently being held in Vakilabad Prison in Mashhad.

A source close to Amini’s family confirmed this information and told HRANA about the judicial proceedings in her cases: “Following her arrest, she faced two separate legal cases, one heard by the Mashhad Revolutionary Court and the other by Criminal Court One. In the case heard by Criminal Court One, she was sentenced to death on charges of ‘insulting the Prophet.’ Initially, the charge against Ms. Amini in this case was described as ‘insulting the Imams,’ but the charge was subsequently changed during the judicial proceedings.”

The source added: “In a separate case, Branch One of the Mashhad Revolutionary Court sentenced Ms. Amini to a total of 12 years, six months, and one day in prison on charges including ‘acting against national security’ and ‘propaganda against the regime.'”

title: Guterres Bids Farewell to a United Nations Under Strain
content:
The outgoing Secretary-General leaves behind unresolved questions of war, representation, finance and climate justice.

By Ramesh Jaura

BERLIN | NEW YORK | 25 September 2026 (IDN) — The Security Council offers the clearest example. It becomes paralysed whenever a conflict touches the interests of a permanent member or a close ally. Russia can block action over Ukraine. The United States can block measures it considers unacceptable to Israel. China, France and Britain retain the same privilege.

This imbalance has become increasingly difficult to defend. Africa has 54 UN members and accounts for a large share of the Council’s work, yet it has no permanent seat. Guterres has described that exclusion as an injustice.

Most governments publicly support reform. Agreement disappears when they must decide which countries should receive permanent representation, whether new members should hold vetoes and whether the existing five should surrender any authority.

title: Afgaaninaisen katse: Ompelimossa opetellaan uutta ammattia ja luodaan toivoa paremmasta
content:
Setara (nimi muutettu) herää edelleen joka aamu herätyskellonsa helinään. Hän poimii yliopiston opiskelijakorttinsa kirjojensa joukosta, tuijottaa sitä hetken ja asettaa sen hiljaa takaisin paikoilleen.

Oppikirjat makrotaloudesta, tilastotieteestä ja talousjohtamisesta keräävät pölyä hänen pöydällään.

Setarasta piti tulla taloustieteilijä. Hän suunnitteli työskentelevänsä jonakin päivänä Parwanin maakunnan johtavissa talousalan yrityksissä. Jos kaikki olisi sujunut suunnitelmien mukaan, hän olisi jo valmistunut opinnoistaan ja hakenut töitä talousalan koulutettuna osaajana. Mutta jo yli neljän vuoden ajan yliopiston ovet ovat pysyneet kiinni.

Talibanien valtaantulo pysäytti kaiken. Setara on yksi miljoonista afgaanitytöistä, joilta koulutus estettiin. Päätös ei ole vaikuttanut ainoastaan nuorten naisten arkeen ja elinpiiriin vaan kokonaisten sukupolvien tulevaisuuteen. Kun yliopistot suljettiin tytöiltä ja naisilta, unelmat riippumattomuudesta ja valoisammasta tulevaisuudesta sammuivat.

Setara opiskeli taloustieteitä 26-vuotiaana kolmatta vuotta, kun opintomahdollisuudet katkaistiin. Mutta hänen tarinansa ei päättynyt siihen.

title: Apulaisosastopäällikkö Lauratuulia Lehtinen YK:n hätäapurahaston neuvoa-antavaan ryhmään
content:
YK:n pääsihteeri António Guterres on nimennyt apulaisosastopäällikkö, ulkoasiainneuvos Lauratuulia Lehtisen YK:n keskitetyn hätäapurahasto CERF:n neuvoa-antavaan ryhmään kolmivuotiselle kaudelle.

YK:n keskitetty hätäapurahasto CERF (Central Emergency Response Fund) on nopea, strateginen ja tehokas humanitaarinen rahasto, joka reagoi äkillisiin katastrofeihin ja pyrkii varmistamaan riittävän rahoituksen pitkittyneisiin, alirahoitettuihin kriiseihin. YK:n humanitaarisen avun koordinaatiotoimisto OCHA (Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs) hallinnoi rahastoa. Päätökset tuen kanavoimisesta rahaston kautta tekee YK:n hätäapukoordinaattori, humanitaarisista asioista vastaava alipääsihteeri Tom Fletcher.

Suomi on YK:n keskitetyn hätäapurahaston pitkäaikainen tukija. Suomen tuki on viisi miljoonaa euroa vuonna 2026. Lisäksi Suomi valmistelee kuluvalle vuodelle kahden miljoonan euron rahoitusta, jolla hätäapurahasto voi tukea vammaisinkluusion vahvistamista humanitaarisessa avussa.

title: Internal Watchdog says Data Leaks and Bribery Push French Police Misconduct Cases to Five-Year High
content:
Offenses involving corruption, influence peddling, and other integrity violations within the French National Police surged by 45 percent between 2024 and 2025, reaching their highest level in five years, according to an internal oversight report released this week. 

The annual assessment by the General Inspectorate of the National Police, or IGPN, recorded 341 integrity breaches in 2025, up from 234 the previous year. The infractions encompassed bribery, conflicts of interest, embezzlement of public funds, extortion, breaches of professional secrecy, and the unauthorized handling of sensitive personal data.

The oversight agency reported steep increases across three primary categories: unauthorized queries of police databases, which jumped by 80 percent; corruption offenses, which rose by 33 percent; and breaches of professional secrecy, which increased by 25 percent.

Stéphane Hardouin, the head of the IGPN, acknowledged the sharp rise in misconduct. “There was a significant increase in breaches of integrity,” Hardouin said, pointing specifically to the rise in corruption and database misuse.

title: How Else Marie Pade, a Prisoner in World War II, Became Denmark’s First Female Electronic Composer
content: Before she became a composer of electronic music, Else Marie Pade was a sick child listening to the radio. Frequent kidney inflammations consigned her to bed for long periods of time, which would constitute neither her last nor her harshest experience of confinement. She was still young when the Nazis occupied her homeland of Denmark during World War II, and perhaps her youth explains her decision to spit on a column of marching German soldiers. She escaped capture that day, running right into the Danish Resistance, for which she distributed underground newspapers and trained in the use of explosives to cut off the enemy’s telephone lines in the event of an Allied invasion. Arrested by the Gestapo in 1944, she never did get to execute that plan, but her real ambitions turned out to be much larger.

title: Colorado Marijuana Company Voluntarily Recalls Dozens of Contaminated Products Amid State Regulatory Delays
content:
A Colorado manufacturer of a popular brand of marijuana vapes warned dispensaries last week that it is recalling products due to contamination by methylene chloride, a chemical the Environmental Protection Agency has sought to ban for most uses because it can cause cancer.

The recall comes amid a protracted delay in state implementation of expanded testing procedures that would have detected methylene chloride and other solvents that pose health risks.

The manufacturer, StayCon, voluntarily flagged 49 of its products, some of which first went up on dispensary shelves more than a year and a half ago. The recalled items include vapes that go by the brand name Maui Wowie and Grape Gorilla. The recall notice said a “botanically-derived” flavoring compound used in its marijuana vapes contained methylene chloride.

title: Von der Leyen ally slams EU Commission’s AI response
content:
The European Commission has failed to keep pace with AI developments, Axel Voss, a key German conservative lawmaker on tech policy, said in an interview.

An EPP ally of Commission President Ursula von der Leyen in the European Parliament, Voss criticized the way the Commission is enforcing its artificial intelligence rules in the wake of a series of AI hacking incidents, including OpenAI-powered agents going rogue and breaking into the AI company Hugging Face.

“The whole working method of the European Commission is not adapted to these extremely fast-changing … developments,” he said to Anne McElvoy on the Brussels Playbook Week Ender podcast.

The enforcement of the EU’s 2024 AI Act, which mandates that companies take measures to avoid losing control of their models, “is not on the level [where] we would like to have it,” he added.

The comments shine the spotlight on the European Commission’s Artificial Intelligence Office, which was put in charge of enforcing the AI Act in August.

Voss also said the Commission’s overall response to the fast pace of technological developments is lagging, singling out von der Leyen’s State of the Union last week.

title: Nigeria faces the world’s highest projected death toll from super El Niño heat: what could save lives
content:
Researchers at the University of Chicago’s Climate Impact Lab combined temperature forecasts with research on how heat affects death rates in more than 24,000 regions worldwide, and found that the super El Niño could cause an estimated 451,000 additional heat deaths worldwide between now and February 2027. Michael Greenstone and Tamma Carleton were part of the research team along with Genevieve Maricle and Emily Grover-Kopec. They explain why Africa’s Sahel region is projected to be the hardest hit area, and why Nigeria is also projected to be one of the worst hit country. He explains what steps governments need to take now to protect people there.

Africa’s Sahel region is projected to face the greatest loss of life from the heat brought on by this year’s strong El Niño. The Sahel is a belt of dry land stretching across Africa from the Atlantic Ocean to the Red Sea, between the Sahara Desert in the north and tropical savannas in the south. It covers about 3.05 million square kilometres and cuts through parts of Mauritania, Mali, Niger, Chad, Nigeria, Sudan, Senegal and Eritrea.

title: Postdoctoral Researcher’s Project
content:
Dr Jasmin Lukkari is the first person appointed to the position of postdoctoral researcher at the Institute. She studied history, classical philology, and classical archaeology at the Universities of Turku and Helsinki. From 2016 to 2017, she worked on a research project led by Tuomas Heikkilä, a former director of the Institute. Lukkari completed her doctoral dissertation at the Universities of Helsinki and Cologne under a cotutelage agreement in 2023, specialising in Roman Republican history and historiography.

At the Institute, Lukkari will continue the research project she began at the University of Milan. She studies international relations between the senate of the Roman Republic and the Hellenistic East, focusing particularly on descriptions by Polybius, Livy, and other historians of the period. Lukkari examines the emphasis these historians placed on personal relationships, emotions, motives, and individual moral values. Applying narratological methods, she investigates how Polybius and Livy emphasize the importance of these factors in diplomatic relations, how they might reflect different historical realities, and to what extent their purpose is to dramatise the narrative.

title: Satoarvio 2026: ruissato jää pieneksi, hernesato ennätyksellinen
content:
Luonnonvarakeskuksen (Luke) vuoden 2026 toisen satoarvion mukaan Suomen viljasato on keskimääräinen. Hernesadosta puolestaan on tulossa yli satavuotisen tilastointihistorian suurin. Herneen viljelyala on yli nelikertaistunut kymmenessä vuodessa ja on nyt jo kolminkertainen peruna-alaan verrattuna.

Vilja-ala pieneni viime vuodesta noin 70 000 hehtaaria ja jäi hieman alle miljoonaan hehtaariin. Viljaa kasvoi siten reilulla 40 prosentilla peltoalasta.

Tämän vuoden kokonaisviljasadoksi arvioidaan 3,2 miljardia kiloa. Viljasato koostuu neljästä pääviljasta. Tämänhetkisen satoarvion mukaan vehnän ja kauran sadot ovat nousemassa lähes kymmenyksen kymmenen vuoden keskiarvoa suuremmiksi. Pääviljamme ohran sato on puolestaan jäämässä yli kymmenyksen ja ruisleipäviljamme rukiin sato noin neljänneksen keskiarvoa pienemmäksi.

Kuva infogrammina

Rukiin satoarvio on vain noin 62 miljoonaa kiloa, joka ei riitä kattamaan vuosittaista käyttöä. Puuttuvaa ruismäärää voidaan paikata maatilojen ja teollisuuden aiempien vuosien varastoilla sekä tarvittaessa tuonnilla.

content:
Inom utsatt ansökningstid har tjänsten som chef för Kyrkostyrelsens avdelning för ekonomi och ICT sökts av 17 personer. Ansökningstiden gick ut på onsdag 23 september klockan 15. Kyrkostyrelsens ekonomi- och ICT- avdelning sköter ärenden som hör till Kyrkans centralfond och ansvarar för organiseringen och underhållet av kyrkans nationella, Kyrkans centralfonds IT-områdens och Kyrkostyrelsens informationsförvaltning.

Nio sökande vill inte att deras namn offentliggörs.

Utifrån ansökningarna väljer man vilka som går vidare. Enligt planerna besluts 29.9.2026 vilka som går vidare till intervjuer.

I den arbetsgrupp som bereder ärendet och intervjuar de sökande ingår kanslichef Niilo Pesonen och personalchef Sari Kiili. Plenum utnämnde 26.8.2026 inom sig Kari Aakula och Hannu Kallunki till medlemmar i berednings- och intervjugruppen. Sekreterare för gruppen är servicechef Tuija Korva.

Kyrkostyrelsens plenum besluter om tillsättandet av de ledande tjänsterna vid Kyrkostyrelsen.

title: Masennus ei näytä aivoissa samalta kaikilla – tutkijat löysivät viisi erilaista aivoprofiilia
content:
Kaksi ihmistä voi saada saman masennusdiagnoosin, vaikka heidän oireensa ovat hyvin erilaiset. Helsingin yliopiston tutkijat halusivat selvittää, näkyykö sama yksilöllisyys myös aivojen toiminnassa. Näkyi: masennusta sairastavien joukosta erottui viisi ryhmää, joiden aivot toimivat keskenään eri tavoin.

"Erityisen kiinnostavaa oli, kuinka vastakkaisia aivojen toimintamalleja saman masennusdiagnoosin sisältä löytyi. Joillakin henkilöillä aivoalueiden välinen toiminnallinen yhteys oli tavallista voimakkaampaa, toisilla taas heikompaa", sanoo Helsingin yliopiston Neurotieteen tutkimuskeskuksen johtaja Satu Palva tiedotteessa.

Toiminnalliset yhteydet kertovat, kuinka hyvin eri aivoalueet toimivat samanaikaisesti. Ne kuvastavat aivoalueiden välistä viestintää.

Tutkimus julkaistiin Nature Mental Health -lehdessä elokuun lopussa. Siihen osallistui 263 masennusta sairastavaa ja 75 tervettä verrokkia.

Aivotoimintaa mitattiin levossa magnetoenkefalografialla eli MEG:llä. Menetelmä tallentaa heikkoja magneettikenttiä, joita aivojen sähköinen toiminta synnyttää.

title: US: Trump Administration Rejects External Election Observers
content:
(New York) – The Trump administration’s decision not to invite the leading international election observation body to monitor crucial US midterm polls fuels fears of serious human rights concerns around the upcoming elections, Human Rights Watch said today. 

“The US government has long criticized Russia and other governments for dodging external scrutiny of their elections,” said Philippe Bolopion, executive director of Human Rights Watch. “Now the Trump administration is mimicking that behavior.”

The Organization for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE), which has observed every US federal election since 2002, called the decision “regrettable” and “not in line with” US commitments. Just over a month before the elections, the United States is mired in several controversies that raise concerns about the rights of voters, Human Rights Watch said.

The Supreme Court on September 25, 2026, granted an emergency appeal by the Trump administration to overturn a ruling that had temporarily barred the government from using the current version of the Department of Homeland Security’s Systematic Alien Verification for Entitlements (SAVE) database to verify voters’ citizenship.

title: A Pact Against Gold-Plating the Research Exception?
content:
In the State of the EU address last week, Commission President von der Leyen announced, to some applause, the idea of a ‘Pact against gold-plating’.

This refers to when EU Member States implementing EU laws decide to add extra detail to the features of the official Regulation, Directive or other regulatory tool. While some of this is simple drafting to ensure EU laws fit seamlessly into national statute, sometimes it serves other goals, such as advantaging a given sector of that country’s economy.

The problem is that adding such provisions tends to make regulation more difficult to comply with. It also represents a barrier to cross-border collaboration by undermining harmonisation efforts.

Typically, efforts to address gold plating focus on things like product regulation or reporting requirements. However, the way in which national governments have implemented copyright exceptions – often under pressure from the entertainment sector – arguably provides another strong example.

title: Azerbaijan: Authorities must immediately release activist Bahruz Samadov who cut himself during latest court appearance
content:
Reacting to reports that imprisoned Azerbaijani researcher and peace activist Bahruz Samadov harmed himself during a Supreme Court hearing on 25 September, Natalia Nozadze, Amnesty International’s South Caucasus Researcher, said:

“Azerbaijani authorities are obliged to protect and fulfil Bahruz Samadov’s right to health while he remains unjustly imprisoned. While they continue to deny him access to adequate healthcare, including mental health support, his health condition is worsening. The denial of health care, and the restrictions on family contact, may amount to cruel, inhuman or degrading treatment, contrary to Azerbaijan’s international human rights obligations.”

“Bahruz Samadov should not have been imprisoned in the first place. He is serving a 15-year sentence on fabricated ‘high treason’ charges stemming from his peaceful activism, journalism and advocacy for dialogue with Armenia. The Azerbaijani authorities must release him immediately and unconditionally.”

Background

On 25 September, Bahruz Samadov used a sharp object to cut his right arm several times during a break in a Supreme Court hearing on 25 September, according to his lawyer, Zibeyda Sadigova.

title: The Hague Group: South Africa Leads Coalition Against U.S./Israel's "Unilateral Bullying" of the ICC
content:
At the United Nations this week, President Trump repeated his attacks on the International Criminal Court and urged other nations to pull out of the global tribunal. The United States earlier this year imposed sanctions on the president of the ICC and a senior prosecutor who was part of the team that issued an arrest warrant for Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu for crimes against humanity in Gaza, and the Trump administration is reportedly preparing more sanctions against the institution itself. Meanwhile, a coalition of nations has formed to defend international law in solidarity with the people of Palestine under the banner of the Hague Group, which was established last year by Bolivia, Colombia, Cuba, Honduras, Malaysia, Namibia, Senegal and South Africa.

“It’s an absolute low point for the sacred grounds of the United Nations that President Trump has shown up here and attacked the international legal order,” says Varsha Gandikota, executive secretary of the Hague Group.

We also air remarks from South African Foreign Minister Ronald Lamola, who spoke earlier this week at the historic Riverside Church in New York City to urge respect for international law.

title: Poland and Hungary Win the race for EU recovery funds – but only just
content:
The Recovery and Resilience Facility (RRF), the main component of the EU’s €800-billion-plus NextGenerationEU recovery package, is now entering its final phase. Member states had until August 30 to submit their final payment requests, together with evidence that the agreed reforms and investments had been completed. The European Commission has until December 31 to make the remaining payments.

Poland was among the countries facing the greatest delays in accessing the funds. For years, Brussels withheld payments under the EU’s rule-of-law conditionality mechanism, amid a dispute over judicial independence under the previous Law and Justice (PiS) government.

That left Poland with considerably less time to deliver on its commitments — and created a race to complete the programme before the EU funding window closed.

The Recovery and Resilience Facility played a key role in mitigating the economic and social impact of the COVID-19 pandemic while preparing the EU for long-term development.

title: Gen Z’s political divide isn’t really about gender
content:
Progressives risk misreading Generation Z by treating social media, the manosphere and changing gender norms as the main explanation for young people’s political divergence. These forces matter. But the evidence points to something deeper: economic insecurity, institutional distrust and individualisation are shaping an entire generation, even if men and women often express that malaise differently.

When progressives discuss young people, one story increasingly dominates. Young men are drifting to the right because TikTok, YouTube and the manosphere expose them to antifeminist ideas; young women, meanwhile, are becoming more progressive as gender equality becomes more salient to them. There is truth in parts of this story. Recent elections have shown significant gender differences among young voters, particularly in support for the far right. Young men and women also differ in some gender attitudes, while online ecosystems can amplify highly divergent content. But treating gender conflict as the master explanation risks confusing one of the languages through which discontent is expressed with its deeper sources.

title: Support Global Voices’ Spotlight: Big Tech and Authoritarianism
content:
As tech companies have gained nearly unchecked power around the world, they are now intrinsically linked to authoritarian states

Originally published on Global Voices

Image made via Canva Pro. All images are from Canva or in the public domain.

Technology is deeply interwoven into almost every aspect of modern life. Much of this technology has at least the potential for positive impacts in terms of human connectedness and democratization; indeed, Global Voices is built on the premise that we can use the digital connectivity of the internet to share stories, build empathy, and create community across both physical and cultural-linguistic distances. 

But the same dynamics that concentrate power and wealth in the world have led to the massive accumulation of Big Tech: corporations so large, so multinational, and so entangled in the functioning of what we have come to consider basic services of communications — from telcos and internet providers to social media and other platforms for communication — that they have disproportionate power and influence over governments as well as over the lives, attention, and finances of individual people.

title: Report on the Execution of a Prisoner in Sepidar Prison, Ahvaz
content:
According to HRANA, the news agency of Human Rights Activists in Iran, a prisoner’s death sentence was carried out at Sepidar Prison in Ahvaz.

HRANA has confirmed the identity of the prisoner as Seyed Sadegh Mousavi, 43, married, father of one child, and a resident of Ramshir County. His execution was carried out on August 24, 2026.

Based on information received by HRANA, Mr. Mousavi was arrested approximately four years ago on murder charges and subsequently sentenced to death by a criminal court.

At the time of this report, his execution has not been announced by prison officials or the relevant authorities.

According to HRA’s Annual Report, in 2025 at least 2,063 citizens, including 61 women and 2 juvenile offenders, were executed. Of these, the sentences of 11 individuals were carried out in public. During the same period, 172 other individuals were sentenced to death.

title: Iran and the United States Find a Narrow Opening in New York
content:
Indirect exchanges through Qatar have revived diplomacy, although the two governments remain far apart

By Jamshed Baruah

NEW YORK | 25 September 2026 (IDN) – The annual United Nations gathering is often dismissed as a succession of speeches. Much of its diplomacy, however, takes place outside the General Assembly Hall, in private rooms, hotel meetings and messages carried between governments that cannot yet speak face to face.

That less visible role became evident when Iranian and American officials resumed indirect contact in New York. Qatar relayed messages in the first known diplomatic engagement between the two countries since a ceasefire collapsed in July.

No agreement emerged. A senior Iranian official acknowledged that the two sides remained far apart. Even so, renewed contact offered a small interruption in the cycle of military threats, sanctions and retaliatory action.

Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian told the General Assembly on 23 September that his country would not submit to pressure. His address followed President Donald Trump’s warning that Iran could face annihilation if an agreement were not reached.

title: Guns, Camouflage, and Facebook: How Colombia’s Biggest ‘Narcoinfluencer’ Weaponized Social Media
content:
Nain Pérez had all the qualities a Gen-Z influencer could ask for. 

With an easy smile and thick black hair cut into a stylish hi-top fade, the 27-year-old Colombian built a huge following on Facebook, Instagram, and TikTok by sharing eye-catching images of a high-flying lifestyle: fast motorcycles, big cars, and a beautiful girlfriend known as “Bebecita.”

But behind the romantic snapshots and aspirational memes was a darker reality: Pérez, who went by the alias Bendito Menor (“Little Blessing”), also openly broadcast his role as a rising member of the Self-Defense Forces of the Sierra Nevada, an illegal armed group better known by its Spanish abbreviation ACSN. 

Although he wasn’t the most powerful member of the ACSN — one of several armed groups in Colombia that profit from crimes like drug trafficking and extortion — he was easily the most famous, with a huge fan base that hung on his every move.

title: Across the Country, Youth Prisons Are Closing. This State Is Building More.
content:
Across the country, states have been shuttering their youth prisons as juvenile crime has plummeted and research shows the facilities are not effective at keeping youth out of trouble after release. From 2000 to 2022, the number of the highest-security facilities for kids has dropped by more than 40%, the most recent federal data shows.

In contrast, Tennessee’s Department of Children’s Services has budgeted $360 million to build two new facilities with a total of up to 256 new beds for youth. Construction is set to begin this fall, and they are expected to open in 2028 and 2029. 

According to Tennessee officials, the state doesn’t have enough space for kids who courts have found committed crimes. In the last few years, it has held dozens of teens overnight in temporary places, including, at one point, office buildings. In an emailed response to WPLN and ProPublica, the agency attributed the lack of bed space to a number of factors, including teens’ needs for specific mental health services and temporary staffing issues in its facilities. And it said that national trends “do not determine” whether Tennessee has enough youth beds available.

title: Ian Berry’s Sharpeville images exposed apartheid violence to the world
content:
The influential veteran photojournalist Ian Berry passed away on 13 September 2026. He covered conflicts across the world, but is best known for the photographs he made that documented the Sharpeville massacre in South Africa.

The massacre took place on 21 March 1960 when police opened fire without warning on a crowd of protesters, killing 91 people, many of whom were shot in the back as they fled from the gunfire.

On the day, around 5,000 people gathered outside a police station in Sharpeville, not far from Johannesburg. They had come there in response to a call by the Pan-Africanist Congress to protest against passbooks. These were documents the apartheid state forced all Black South Africans to carry to restrict and control their movements.

Apartheid was a racist ideology implemented by the National Party when it took power in South Africa in 1948. The government passed a series of laws, including the Group Areas Act and the Population Registration Act, that were designed to ensure white supremacy.

Read more: Sharpeville: research on 1960 South African massacre shows the number of dead and injured was massively undercounted

title: DH välipalat for early career researchers
content:
In 2025 we launched a series of discussions among early-career researchers in social sciences and humanities to facilitate peer-support and network opportunities for doctoral and early career stage researchers working with similar methods or types of data. The community now has its own . These “välipalat” or evening snacks were inspired by Prof. Meredith Martin, head of the  at Princeton and scholar of historical poetics. In a  at the 2024 DARIAH Annual event, she made a compelling account of the emotional practices involved in creating a DH department. Frustration, incomprehension and helplessness were some feelings that described the fact that humanists were worked up about data. These feelings were the first stepping stone towards building humanities infrastructures. 

The process that followed could be summarized as knocking on doors. Collecting experiences and stumbling blocks from peers empowered professor Martin to knock on higher doors delivering their needs in a volume that administration and funding bodies could not deny. That is how she built an infrastructure to start curing “digital helplessness”.

title: She came for the books and became a Wikimedian
content:
Jyoti Chiring began editing Assamese Wikisource after retiring from a career in nursing. She is now an active Wikimedian. This blog post stems from the conversation I had with her, while we were roommates at WikiConference India 2026. I was meeting her for the first time there, and she was kind enough to share her story with me, which I promised her will I share with the world. 

Jyoti Chiring did not join the Wikimedia movement because of free knowledge, or the encyclopedia, or anything so abstract. She joined because of books.

She had known a neighbour sitting with a laptop, and they spoke often enough in person for her to take the freedom to ask her what she was doing with it.

“She said, ‘I am working in Wikimedia as a volunteer.”

Jyoti immediately decided that she wants to do this thing like her neighbour. She had just transitioned from a very busy nursing superintendent to a retired mother, and the stillness of her retired life was making her wanting to do more in life.

title: Trump’s US ratings drop to new record low as Democrats become clear favourites in both chambers of Congress
content:
In Nate Silver’s aggregate of national polls, Donald Trump’s net approval has dropped to a new record low of -23.

In his forecast model, Democrats are the clear favourites to gain control of the US federal Senate at November 3 midterm elections, and overwhelming favourites to gain control of the House of Representatives.

If disruption caused by the Iran war continues until the midterm elections, with increased petrol prices and inflation, Republicans are likely to lose control of both the House and the Senate, perhaps with huge losses.

However, if the disruption eases again and petrol prices fall back before the midterms, I believe Republicans will do better than they are now and may retain control of the Senate.

I can say this because Trump’s net approval and the generic ballot were better for Republicans in early September, soon after a low in petrol prices.

In analyst Nate Silver’s aggregate of US national polls, Trump’s net approval is at a new record low -23.0. Currently, 60.4% disapprove of his performance and 37.4% approve.

Trump’s net approval was -19.7 in my September 14 article. It had improved to -18.7 on September 4 before falling back.

title: Ethiopia: Indiscriminate Airstrike in Tigray
content:
(Nairobi) – An apparent Ethiopian government airstrike on a residential compound in Ethiopia’s northern Tigray region on August 20, 2026, should be investigated as a possible war crime, Human Rights Watch said today. The attack wounded 13 civilians, including seven children. 

The airstrike hit the Daero neighborhood of Mekelle, Tigray’s regional capital, which had no evident military targets, making the strike unlawfully indiscriminate. Ethiopian authorities should impartially and transparently investigate the attack, prosecute those responsible for any wrongdoing, and adequately compensate the victims. 

“The resumption of hostilities in northern Ethiopia heightens concerns about unlawful attacks and the grave threat posed to civilians,” said Laetitia Bader, deputy Africa director at Human Rights Watch. “To prevent further harm to civilians, the Ethiopian military needs to abide by the laws of war and ensure that they take all feasible precautions before carrying out any attack.”

title: Niger Rejects Key Rights Recommendations at UN Review
content:
Niger has rejected key recommendations raised by United Nations member countries during its Universal Periodic Review (UPR) earlier this year, including calls to address arbitrary detention, discrimination against lesbian, gay, bisexual and transgender (LGBT) people, and accountability for serious human rights violations. 

The UPR is a UN Human Rights Council process in which the human rights records of member states are reviewed by other member countries every five years.

On September 1, Niger’s military junta responded to the 265 recommendations made in May by 97 UN member countries and accepted 254 of them, including commitments to strengthen civilian protection and ensure security forces receive training on international human rights and humanitarian law.

The junta however rejected 11 recommendations addressing some of the country’s most pressing rights concerns, including to reverse its June decision to start the withdrawal process from the International Criminal Court (ICC). Leaving the ICC risks depriving victims of grave international crimes a last resort to seek justice and remedies.

title: Playing video games with my 22-year-old son has brought me to tears | Dominik Diamond
content:
I’ve been holed up in an flat, affectionately dubbed the ‘brotel’, with my son for weeks – and we’ve revisited the first game we ever played together

I have spent the last three weeks living with my 22-year-old son in a two-bedroom flat he has dubbed the ”brotel”. We cook curries and watch Lanterns. We barbecue meat and analyse Tarantino movies. We get pizza and we play video games. Boy, do we play video games!

The first game I ever played in co-op with him was Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 2 in 2009, when he was five. He wasn’t the most accomplished sidekick, not so great at placing a mobile gun turret while under fire from what seems like a bazillion enemy soldiers, but we had a laugh. It started the video game bond between us before his sister introduced him to Banjo-Kazooie and Rayman, and he stopped being a preschool warmonger. Probably for the best. So how would it be tackling the same game nearly two decades later?

title: Choppy Waters: Caspian War Drones Proliferate
content:
If the future of war was predicted by anyone, then it was Azerbaijan. It used unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) to devastating effect in breaking the long deadlock with Armenia over the enclave of Nagorno-Karabakh. That was in 2020, two years before Russia’s all-out invasion of Ukraine. So it was notable when Azerbaijani President Ilham Aliyev visited Navy Forces Headquarters, accompanied by the Defense Minister General Zakir Hasanov, on September 6 to unveil two new unmanned naval platforms: the super-fast, 49 ft-long, Turkish-made SALVO armed uncrewed surface vessel, and the KAYRA maritime kamikaze drone. Both are being manufactured in Azerbaijan, although numbers are unknown.

Littoral powers including Russia and Iran will take note, as will others with an eye on the Caspian. War in Europe and the Middle East have spilled over into the sea this year: Ukraine hit Russian targets in July and September, and similarly Israel struck Iranian military sites and warships. The sea’s immunity from warfare is now gone, even if the five littoral states are at peace.

title: From policy to protection: making human rights count at sea
content:
From policy to protection: making human rights count at sea

As global attention increasingly shifts to the oceans for discussions or solutions for climate, trade, or conservation, the people who live and work at sea remain largely unseen.

Human rights do not stop at the shoreline. Yet for people who live, work, travel, or find themselves in distress at sea, securing those rights can become significantly harder.

Seafarers and fishers can face dangerous or exploitative working conditions. People intercepted at sea may be detained without clear legal safeguards. Passengers, scientists, offshore workers, and migrants can struggle to access medical assistance, or establish who is responsible for their safety. Distance and isolation make abuses harder to detect, while overlapping jurisdictions can make accountability difficult to secure. These abuses often go unnoticed and unpunished, also due to the vastness and isolation of the maritime environment.

title: My Wiki Birthday: My Journey as a Volunteer with Wikimedistas de Bolivia
content: On September 23, my Wikimedia account turned three years old. Although I started out editing slowly and without really knowing what I was doing, now, looking back, I realize that my daily life is filled with wiki projects, wiki skills, wiki people, wikifications, wikirquinchos, and more—including organizing a party to celebrate Wikipedia’s 25th anniversary in La Paz city. And all of this has allowed me to see that, even though I sometimes feel we’re very constrained in this world—where there are many things we “must” do and few we can propose—this is a place that allows for creativity and offers me a universe of possibilities.

title: EC pledges to strengthen member states’ response to security threats
content:
Particular attention should be paid to plans for a new EU security strategy, including proposals for a Security Council and an EU alert mechanism to respond to security threats that do not reach the level of armed aggression. Critics have previously warned that such a move could risk overlapping with NATO security mechanisms.

With the war in Ukraine increasingly affecting Europe’s eastern flank and Russia stepping up its sabotage attacks and drone campaigns, security and defence became the main theme of the European Commission president’s annual address.

This week alone, Poland raised the alarm after Russia struck a train travelling from Kyiv to Warsaw. At the time of the attack, the train was at the Yahodyn railway station, approximately two kilometres from the Ukrainian-Polish border. Shortly afterwards, Prime Minister Donald Tusk warned that such escalations were increasingly approaching the borders of European countries: “The coming weeks and months are expected to be a very intense period in Russia’s activities.”

title: DraftKings Is Using AI to Supercharge the Harms of Online Behavioral Advertising
content: Online sports betting company DraftKings is using AI to target customers who are most likely to place losing bets and respond to gambling promotions. This kind of targeting is a form of online behavioral advertising, which is when companies personalize the ads they show you based on the data they’ve collected about you. The more data a company has, the more personalized the ad can be. While DraftKings is using AI to supercharge the harmful effects of online behavioral advertising, EFF has long argued that all behavioral advertising should be banned.

title: Amnesty: ICE:n toiminta muuttunut yhä väkivaltaisemmaksi – Yhdysvaltain maahanmuuttovirasto on lakkautettava
content:
Yhdysvaltain maahanmuuttovalvonta on yhä militarisoidumpaa ja väkivaltaisempaa. Amnestyn uusi raportti (liitteenä) dokumentoi laajamittaisia väärinkäytöksiä neljässä laajassa operaatiossa Chicagossa, Minneapolis–Saint Paulissa, New Orleansissa ja Washingtonin pääkaupunkiseudulla.

ICE:n, rajavartiolaitoksen ja muiden liittovaltion viranomaisten toimintaan liittyy muun muassa järjestelmällistä etnistä profilointia, mielivaltaisia pidätyksiä, häirintää, pelottelua, perusteetonta ja liiallista voimankäyttöä sekä epäinhimillisiä olosuhteita pidätyskeskuksissa.

Amnestyn tutkijat haastattelivat 154 ihmistä eri puolilla Yhdysvaltoja ja analysoivat video- ja kuvamateriaalia. Väärinkäytökset toistuivat eri puolilla maata riippumatta valtaapitävästä puolueesta tai muista paikallisista olosuhteista. Raportin mukaan kyse ei ole yksittäisistä ylilyönneistä, vaan laajemmasta toimintamallista.

Trumpin toisen presidenttikauden aikana ICE:n ja rajavartiolaitoksen agentit ovat ampuneet ainakin 22 ihmistä, joista 11 on kuollut. Amnestyn tutkimista tapauksista kolmessa voi olla kyse laittomasta teloituksesta.

title: A gradual path to recovery: How the Polirone Monastic Complex of San Benedetto Po in Italy became a model for community-led conservation
content:
When an earthquake struck the Northern Italian regions of Emilia-Romagna and Lombardy in 2012, the Polirone Monastic Complex of San Benedetto Po suffered extensive damage. The loss was twofold: an impressive 16th-century Renaissance architectural structure was devastated, and its surrounding community lost access to one of their most important cultural spaces.

Since being listed among the 7 Most Endangered heritage sites in Europe for 2013, the restoration and recovery of the monastery has become an example of heritage restoration, community in action and resilience, recognised with both a European Heritage Award / Europa Nostra Award and a Grand Prix 2026 in the category Conservation and Adaptive Reuse.

For this Impact Story, Europa Nostra sat down with Federica Guidetti, Curator of Polironiano Civic Museum, who was involved in the nomination of the site for the 7 Most Endangered Programme, to learn more about how this community raised a monastery from the rubble.

title: Arts and mental health in wartime: Exchanging experiences with Ukraine
content:
How can arts and cultural activities support people living with trauma, grief, displacement and the continuing pressure of war? And what can mental health professionals across the Baltic Sea Region learn from the experience of Ukrainian communities?

These questions were at the heart of the third international meeting of the Arts for Health and Well-being Network (ArtWell NET), held in Kolomyia, Ukraine. Partners from Ukraine, Sweden, Poland and Estonia came together with local psychologists, educators and cultural professionals to exchange experience and explore how arts-based approaches can support mental health, recovery and community resilience.

For communities in Ukraine, mental health support is needed in circumstances of continuing uncertainty and loss. Veterans, military families, internally displaced people, children and professionals supporting others may all face the psychological consequences of war.

Clinical services remain essential, but they cannot meet every need alone. Safe group activities, trusted local networks and opportunities for creativity and connection can also help people regain a sense of belonging, express difficult emotions and rebuild everyday routines.

title: Trinidad & Tobago’s Special Operations Bill and the geography of development
content:
Once the state identifies an area, it must also ask, ‘What else is known about [it]?’

Originally published on Global Voices

Trinidad and Tobago’s capital, Port of Spain, with its historic lighthouse. Photo by Dan Lunberg on Flickr (CC BY 2.0).

Trinidad and Tobago’s Special Operations Bill 2026 is primarily a response to crime and insecurity. It establishes seven policing districts in which special operations could be conducted, with police officers able to receive military assistance from the Defence Force. The proposed legislation also provides for closed areas, curfews, cordons, searches, reporting requirements and training in areas including human rights, use of force and community engagement.

title: Mohammad Naderi Sentenced to Death
content:
According to HRANA, Mohammad Naderi, a prisoner held in Greater Tehran Prison, has been sentenced to death.

Based on information received by HRANA, Naderi was sentenced to death by Branch 23 of the Tehran Revolutionary Court on charges of “espionage.”

He was arrested by security forces amid war-related security developments and transferred to Greater Tehran Prison.

HRANA’s investigation into the details of his case, including the evidence cited by the court and whether he has had access to a lawyer of his choosing, is ongoing.

title: Ukraine and the Security Council’s Unresolved Contradiction
content:
The body charged with maintaining international peace remains constrained when a permanent member is involved in the war.

By J. Nastranis

NEW YORK | 24 September 2026 (IDN) – The warning that the war in Ukraine has entered a dangerous new phase may sound familiar after more than five years of fighting. Repetition, however, should not dull its meaning.

Attacks are becoming more intense. Energy installations and transport routes remain vulnerable. Long-range weapons allow both sides to strike far beyond the front. Each escalation increases the possibility that the conflict will cross another border, damage a nuclear facility or draw neighbouring states more directly into the fighting.

A high-level meeting of the United Nations Security Council on 23 September considered these dangers. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy also used his General Assembly address to argue that Russia’s actions were making the wider world less secure.

The meeting once again revealed the Council’s deepest weakness. Russia is both a permanent member of the body responsible for maintaining international peace and a party to the war under discussion.

title: Cross-border journalism comes to Budapest
content:
Investigative journalists from across Europe and beyond gathered in the Hungarian capital on September 17 and 18 for UNCOVERED 2026, the annual conference of the Investigative Journalism for Europe (IJ4EU) programme. The event brought together reporters, editors and media experts to examine the pressures facing cross-border journalism and the practical challenges of doing it.

Around 150 participants from 32 countries attended the sixth edition of the conference, hosted by Goethe-Institut Hungary, for a day and a half of panels, workshops, mentoring and exchanges on subjects ranging from government pressure and journalist safety to newsroom sustainability, freelance working conditions and the impact of major investigations.

At the centre of the programme was a question that ran through much of the conference: how can investigative journalists work across borders, withstand mounting political and financial pressure, and produce reporting that leads to meaningful change?

Here is a brief recap of UNCOVERED 2026, told through pictures.
