title: Syksyn apurahahaku alkaa
content:
Journalistisen kulttuurin edistämissäätiön syksyn apurahahaku alkaa 28. syyskuuta. Nyt haettavat apurahat on tarkoitettu vuoden 2027 hankkeisiin.

Jokesin apurahoja myönnetään esimerkiksi ammattitaidon täydentämiseen, tutkimukseen, kieli- ja opintomatkoihin ja ammattikuvaa syventävään työskentelyyn. Työskentelyapurahoja myönnetään tieteen ja taiteen tekemiseen, esimerkiksi näyttelyihin ja kirjojen kirjoittamiseen. Lisäksi myönnetään 3 000 euron työskentelyapurahoja journalistisiin hankkeisiin. Opiskelijoille myönnetään vain opiskelijastipendejä opinnäytetyön tekemiseen.

Säätiön kahden viikon kielikurssit järjestetään keväällä 2027 Bordeaux’ssa, Malagassa, Lontoossa, Tallinnassa (venäjän kieli) ja Tukholmassa. Tässä apurahahaussa voit hakea kielikurssien lisäksi säätiön Kolumnipajaan, joka järjestetään tammikuussa 2027 Helsingissä.

Jokesin jakamat apurahat rahoitetaan pääsääntöisesti Kopioston Journalistiliitolle maksamilla Kopiosto-korvauksilla. Kopiosto kerää näitä korvauksia tekijöiden antamien valtakirjojen nojalla. Lue tästä, millaisesta työstä Jokesille kertyy Kopiosto-korvauksia.

title: Oulankajoen varrelle syntyy uusi Luolakallion luonnonsuojelualue
content:
Luonnonperintösäätiö osti syyskuun alussa suojeluun 42 hehtaaria metsää Sallan Oulangan kylästä. Oulankajoen keskijuoksulla sijaitseva Luolakallion luonnonsuojelualue sisältää vanhoja luonnonmetsiä, arvokkaita jokivarsimaisemia sekä valtakunnallisesti merkittävään Isokurun kallioalueeseen liittyviä luontoarvoja.

Suojeltava alue sijaitsee Oulankajoen pohjoispuolella molemmin puolin Kuusamo-Salla-tietä. Oulankajoen varren rinnemetsät ovat vanhaa, paikoin jopa 200-vuotiasta luonnonmetsää, pääosin kuusikkoa. Muu osa alueesta koostuu eri-ikäisrakenteisista, pääosin mäntyvaltaisista metsistä, joita on aiemmin hyödynnetty metsätaloudessa. Lisäksi alueeseen kuuluu noin kuusi hehtaaria avointa tai puoliavointa suota sekä pieni korpilaikku ja lähde.

”Tien itäpuoleinen Oulankajoen ranta on kallioinen ja paikoin hyvin jyrkkä. Maisema on jylhä ja muistuttaa paljon muutaman kilometrin päässä alkavan Oulangan kansallispuiston joenvarsimaisemaa”, ihastelee Luonnonperintösäätiön suojelupäällikkö Ari-Pekka Auvinen.

title: Tutkimus: Uskomus, jonka mukaan kapitalismi kuroo globaalit tuloerot umpeen, ei pidä paikkansa
content:
Kaikki maailman maat ovat samalla kehittymismatkalla, mutta eri vaiheissa. Tämä ajatus on perustana, kun puhutaan niin sanotusta tuloerojen kiinni kuromisen teoriasta, englanniksi convergence theory. 

Konvergenssiteorian mukaan tuloerot kuroutuvat ennen pitkää umpeen talouskasvun ansiosta.  

Uusi tutkimus kuitenkin osoittaa, että empiirisesti tämä teoria ei pidä paikkansa eikä kiinnikuromista ole tapahtunut niin kovaan tahtiin kuin vallalla oleva narratiivi on viime vuosina hehkuttanut. 

Tarkastelemalla dataa nähdään, että globaalit tuloerot ovat itse asiassa vain kasvaneet viime vuosikymmeninä.   

Ydin, eli maailman rikkaimmat maat, rohmusi 4–10 kertaa enemmän tuloja kuin periferia.

title: Suomi edistää Venäjän hyökkäyssodan vastuuvelvollisuutta
content:
Hallitus on torstaina 24. syyskuuta antanut eduskunnalle hallituksen esitykset Ukrainaan kohdistuvaa hyökkäysrikosta käsittelevää erityistuomioistuinta koskevan sopimuksen sekä Ukrainan kansainvälisen vaadekomission perustamissopimuksen hyväksymiseksi ja voimaansaattamiseksi.

”Vastuuvelvollisuus on yksi oikeudenmukaisen ja kestävän rauhan edellytyksistä. Vastuuvelvollisuusmekanismien kautta varmistamme, että Venäjä ja sen johto vastaavat kansainvälisen oikeuden vastaisten tekojensa oikeudellisista seurauksista. Lisäksi autamme Ukrainaa ja uhreja saamaan oikeutta ja hyvitystä Venäjän hyökkäyssodan aiheuttamista vahingoista”, ulkoministeri Elina Valtonen toteaa.   

Sopimuksilla perustettavat vastuuvelvollisuusmekanismit edistävät sekä rikosoikeudellisen vastuun toteutumista hyökkäysrikoksesta että Venäjän vastuun toteutumista hyökkäyssodan aiheuttamista vahingoista. Molemmat mekanismit perustetaan Euroopan neuvoston yhteyteen ja niiden toimipaikka tulee olemaan Haagissa. Suomi on osallistunut aktiivisesti molempien sopimusten valmistelu- ja neuvotteluprosesseihin.

title: Now Entering: The Era Of Bleh
content:
It’s 9 a.m. Monday morning. To start his week, Lukas Weber, a 28-year-old copywriter for a mid-sized SaaS company, first checks on the small army of AI agents he has built and now manages. It’s been part of his daily routine since his company’s “AI-first” mandate at the start of the year.

His agents have been busy. One agent has pulled in all the industry news from the past week and combined it with customer calls to identify potential newsletter topics. That agent has since handed off its findings to a copywriting agent that has written drafts for Weber to review and send out. Another has identified prospective clients visiting the company website and, based on their activity, sent each a custom proposal. Another agent has analyzed the data from a recent campaign and, noticing some concerning trends, reached out to Weber to take a look. Yet another has responded to unread emails, and the drafts sit ready to review in Weber’s inbox.

title: Bosnian Police Officer Dies by Suicide Following Raid
content:
A Bosnian police officer died by suicide Wednesday after authorities searched his office during a multi-city anti-trafficking operation, officials and local media reported. The State Investigation and Protection Agency (SIPA) stated Thursday the suspect suffered a self-inflicted gunshot wound during raids across Sarajevo, Doboj, and Bratunac targeting an organized crime network involved in arms and drug trafficking.

Local investigative outlet Istraga identified the suspect as a Sarajevo Canton police officer who shot himself inside the Ilijaš police station following the search, saying he was allegedly tied to the notorious Swedish criminal ring known as Foxtrot. According to Istraga, the operation was coordinated with Europol to target a ring allegedly supplying weapons to the gang led by Majid Rawa. Local media also linked the operation to last week's record bust in the same municipality.

During the operation, SIPA said officers seized nine hunting rifles, five pistols, about 190 rounds of ammunition, and forged documents allegedly used to fraudulently issue firearms permits and facilitate illegal weapons sales.

title: The Long, Strange History of Tarot Cards: From the 14th Century to Modern Times
content:
We have any number of reasons for difficulty getting to sleep, not least worries about the future. This is hardly a recent phenomenon, and indeed practices meant to clarify the nature of events to come may be older than civilization itself. In fact, many of us moderns trust the old ways of fortune-telling more than the new. Take the cards of the Tarot, often featured here on Open Culture, whose recognizable European form dates back to at least the fourteenth century. But as explained in the new video above from YouTube channel Bedtime & Historian, their pre-history begins longer ago and farther away, with the invention of the playing card itself in Tang-Dynasty China. For Tarot decks weren’t originally a means of glimpsing the future, but of passing time in the present.

In the 400 years or so between the civilizational journey playing cards made along the Silk Road and their first employment as a divination tool by French occultists, many a game of Tarot — or tarocchi, Tarock, and so on — took place in Europe. Monetary stakes, and sometimes considerable ones, were not unknown, which drew the ire of both state and Church authorities.

title: Neuromoninainen museo – Neurovähemmistöt muovaavat museota
content:
Neuromoninaisuus on ajattelutapa ja liike, jonka ytimessä on ajatus siitä, että kaikki neurotyypit ovat osa ihmisen luonnollista neurobiologista vaihtelua. Viime vuosikymmenten aikana tämä ajattelutapa on muovannut käsityksiämme neurovähemmistöistä. Se ei ole vaikuttanut ainoastaan siihen, miten ymmärrämme ihmisten neurobiologista moninaisuutta, vaan myös siihen, miten toimimme tämä moninaisuus huomioiden.

Neurovähemmistöillä tarkoitetaan neurobiologisen vähemmistön muodostavia ryhmiä. Näihin ryhmiin kuuluvat esimerkiksi autismi, ADHD, dysleksia ja OCD sekä aivovammat. Neurovähemmistöihin kuuluvat ihmiset ovat usein kokeneet elämänsä aikana syrjintää, häirintää, vähättelyä ja epäasiallista kohtelua. Osa on kokenut myös väkivaltaa.

Epäreilu kohtelu ei johdu ainoastaan yksittäisistä tilanteista tai kohtaamisista, vaan rakenteista, jotka ovat asettaneet neurovähemmistöihin kuuluvat eriarvoiseen asemaan yhteiskunnassa. Lisäksi siihen ovat vaikuttaneet arvot ja asenteet, jotka ovat muovanneet sitä, miten olemme aiemmin ymmärtäneet, tai jättäneet ymmärtämättä, neuromoninaisuutta.

title: Presidentti Stubbin valtiovierailulla Luxemburgissa esillä Euroopan turvallisuus
content:
Tasavallan presidentin kanslia
Tiedote 59/2026
24.9.2026

Tasavallan presidentti Alexander Stubb ja hänen puolisonsa Suzanne Innes-Stubb tekevät valtiovierailun Luxemburgiin 29.–30. syyskuuta 2026 suurherttua Guillaumen ja suurherttuatar Stéphanien kutsusta.

Vierailulla ovat esillä Suomen ja Luxemburgin kahdenväliset suhteet ja kaupallistaloudellinen yhteistyö, globaalihaasteet, kokonaisturvallisuus ja Euroopan vahvistaminen sekä Venäjän laiton hyökkäyssota Ukrainassa.  

Suurherttua Guillaume ja suurherttuatar Stéphanie ottavat presidenttiparin vastaan virallisin seremonioin palatsissaan tiistaina 29. syyskuuta. Presidenttipari laskee myös seppeleen Luxemburgin kansalliselle solidaarisuusmuistomerkille.

Presidentin ohjelmaan kuuluvat tapaamiset edustajainhuoneen puhemies Claude Wiselerin, pääministeri Luc Friedenin sekä varapääministeri ja ulkoministeri Xavier Bettelin kanssa.

Iltapäivällä presidenttipari ja suurherttuapari tapaavat Luxemburgin pormestari Lydie Polferin kaupungintalolla. Lisäksi presidentti Stubb vierailee Euroopan investointipankissa ja Euroopan unionin tuomioistuimessa Kirchbergissä.

Päivän päättää suurherttuaparin isännöimä illallinen valtiovierailun kunniaksi.

title: How the Smithsonian Became the Latest Front in Trump’s Culture War
content:
In November 2021, the Smithsonian’s National Museum of American History opened an exhibit called “The Electric Dr. Franklin,” describing “Benjamin Franklin’s pioneering contributions to electrical science.” The exhibit explained that, prior to becoming an abolitionist, he had enslaved people in his household. “Benjamin Franklin’s remarkable scientific accomplishments were, in part, enabled by slavery,” it declared. 

The exhibit speculated that Franklin may have used enslaved people in his electrical research. “Franklin wrote about experiments in which he took shocks and used family and friends in these ways, although he seldom identified who in particular assisted him,” stated the exhibit, which closed in 2025 but can still be found online. “Indentured servants and enslaved people in his household could also have been used, although we may never know for certain.”

title: Svenska institutet finansierar nya samarbeten för Ukrainas återuppbyggnad och EU-integration
content:
Årets utlysning fick rekordstort gensvar. Totalt inkom 137 ansökningar från universitet, civilsamhällesorganisationer, företag, stiftelser, myndigheter och kommuner. Efter en noggrann bedömning har 26 projekt beviljats finansiering.

De finansierade projekten omfattar tre områden där samarbete mellan svenska och ukrainska organisationer bedöms kunna bidra till Ukrainas fortsatta utveckling:

  • Innovation och entreprenörskap
  • Transparens, ansvarsutkrävande och arbete mot korruption
  • Jämställdhet

    • – Det stora intresset visar att det finns ett starkt engagemang hos organisationer i både Sverige och Ukraina att bidra till landets återuppbyggnad och långsiktiga utveckling, säger Kurt Bratteby, chef för avdelningen för internationella relationer på Svenska institutet.

  • EU Compliance Compass leds av Högskolan i Halmstad tillsammans med ukrainska universitet, expertorganisationer och den nationella myndigheten för korruptionsförebyggande arbete. Projektet ska ta fram verktyg, utbildningar och digitala lösningar som stärker arbetet mot korruption och stödjer anpassningen till EU:s regelverk.

title: EU’s top AI adviser urges commissioners to use the technology to fix bloc’s economy
content:
BRUSSELS — The EU should focus less on winning the race to build artificial intelligence and more on how to deploy it to turn around the bloc’s sluggish productivity, the European Commission’s chief AI adviser told commissioners.

The technology is Europe’s best chance to accelerate growth in a range of sectors — including health, agriculture, transport, defense and manufacturing — Jim Hagemann Snabe, the EU’s new special envoy for industrial AI, told the bloc’s 27 commissioners at a Sept. 4 seminar, according to two Commission officials. They were granted anonymity to discuss the private briefing.

The EU is trying to capture the economic gains of rapidly advancing AI even as it grapples with the technology’s risks to jobs, security and society. Europe’s leaders should not worry too much about leading the development of frontier AI models, but should “be the ones who draw the greatest value from it” while managing its dangers, Commission President Ursula von der Leyen said in her State of the Union speech last week.

title: Launch of UK’s ‘largest AI supercomputer’ delayed by power supply problems
content:
Datacentre hailed by government was supposed to start operating next year but may be held back into mid-2030s

A huge datacentre project hailed by the UK government will miss its launch date next year and could be delayed into the mid-2030s.

The site in Loughton, Essex, was described as the country’s largest AI supercomputer when it was announced in 2025, but power supply problems mean it now faces a lengthy wait before coming online.

title: From east to west: Why Turkey is playing both sides
content:
Less than two months after his government hosted the NATO summit — which was framed as proof of Turkey’s pivotal role in transatlantic security — President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan has proposed full Turkish membership in the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation, an entity that has been described as being anti-NATO or a “rogue NATO.”

The apparent contradiction was striking. Turkey has belonged to NATO since 1952 and remains a European Union candidate. In contrast, the China- and Russia-led Shanghai Cooperation Organisation, which has included Iran since 2023, projects an alternative, non-western vision of international order.

This revives a familiar question: is Turkey pivoting from west to east?

The question assumes a world divided into coherent blocs. In reality, partially overlapping and competing international orders co-exist, each with its own institutions, rules and visions of global authority. Turkey is simply asserting its autonomy by moving across their boundaries.

The post-Cold War vision of a single global order centred on western institutions is increasingly difficult to sustain. NATO co-exists with emerging power coalitions and regional or issue-specific partnerships.

title: UN chief says world’s biggest problem is the changing way power is used – Donald Trump’s speech confirms his diagnosis
content:
UN secretary-general, António Guterres, used his final address to the general assembly to recast the world’s crises as a single problem. War, inequality, the climate emergency and artificial intelligence, he argued, are not separate crises but chapters of the same story. That story, as he told it, is the story of power: who has it, who is denied it, how it is used and how it is changing.

Guterres identified three shifts. Among states, new centres of economic, political and technological influence have emerged. Power is also moving away from governments to a handful of private corporations and individuals. And humans are increasingly handing power to machines, with AI agents going rogue and lethal autonomous weapons becoming a military reality.

These shifts put the use of power to the test: power over war and peace, the power that concentrates wealth and drives inequality, the power fuelling climate chaos, and the power unleashed by artificial intelligence.

title: Who Will Steward Humanity’s Public Data? Collective Global Stewardship for the Long Horizon
content:
On September 10, 2026, Jacqueline J. Dearborn, Library Innovation Lab Fellow, gave a virtual talk about the Public Data Project’s International Data Infrastructure Research and Development effort. The transcript below has been lightly edited for clarity.

Hello everyone, before I get started, I want to give a shout-out to Molly Hardy and Jack Cushman at the Harvard Library Innovation Lab for giving me this opportunity to reflect on some of the most pressing challenges of our time.

With Jennifer Chapman as my counterpart, we’ve spearheaded the Public Data Infrastructure Research and Development project and through this work, we’ve gotten the chance to zoom way, way, way out and take a look at the global public data landscape.

Obviously this is a very huge, thorny, and complex topic. Much larger than any one talk could possibly resolve. So today, I share some preliminary insights that I hope will help us think together about public data infrastructure, long-term stewardship, and collective responsibility. In this spirit, I hope this talk is less of an ending and more of a beginning for all of us that spurs many future conversations to come.

title: Faculty of Pharmacy hosts Sustainable Pharmacy Summer School for the first time in Finland
content:
The summer school has previously taken place at the University of Freiburg (2022 and 2024), Kiel University (2023), and Martin Luther University Halle-Wittenberg (2025). Participants included representatives from academia, agencies, the healthcare sector and the pharmaceutical industry. "Four days of insightful presentations and engaging discussions," was how the organisers summed up the event.

The programme combined expert lectures, group discussions, a poster session, and plenty of opportunities for international networking. Each day had its own theme:

  • Monday – Planetary Health. The day set the stage by defining health within the broader context of planetary health, addressing the threat posed by climate change to shared health as well as silent pandemics, along with ethical considerations and equity in access to healthcare and pharmaceuticals.
  • Tuesday – Pharmaceutical Development. The focus was on sustainable practices in pharmaceutical development, including formulations and manufacturing processes, the "sustainable-by-design" approach, and advances in sustainable analytical chemistry.

title: Suomen merimetsokanta pieneni kuusi prosenttia
content:
Suomessa laskettiin kesällä 2026 yhteensä noin 30 100 merimetson pesää. Pesimäkanta pieneni edellisvuodesta noin kuusi prosenttia eli vajaalla 2 000 pesällä.

"Merimetson pesimäkanta notkahti kahden edellisvuoden tasosta. Vuosina 2024 ja 2025 Suomessa laskettiin noin 32 000 merimetson pesää. Kannan laskuun on voinut vaikuttaa viime talven ankaruus, sillä merimetsojen havaittiin kärsineen talvimyrskyissä eri puolilla Itämerta," sanoo erikoistutkija Kim Jaatinen Suomen ympäristökeskuksen tiedotteessa.

Selkämerellä laskettiin kesällä noin 12 460 merimetson pesää. Suomenlahdella niitä oli noin 10 200, Saaristomerellä 3 600, Merenkurkussa noin 2 000 ja Perämerellä noin 1 750.

Selkämerellä oli ensimmäistä kertaa selvästi enemmän merimetson pesiä kuin muilla merialueilla. Pesämäärä kasvoi siellä edellisvuodesta hieman yli tuhannella.

Suomenlahdella pesämäärä puolestaan pieneni reilulla tuhannella. Saaristomerellä vähennystä oli lähes neljännes, 1 125 pesää, kun taas Perämerellä ja Merenkurkussa määrä pieneni joillain sadoilla.

Sisämaassa merimetso pesi viime vuosien tapaan vain yhdessä yhdyskunnassa Päijät-Hämeessä. Siellä laskettiin hieman yli 20 pesää.

title: WITNESS Launches Its First Regional Deepfake Rapid Response Force in Brazil
content:
The new initiative brings together Brazilian fact-checkers and forensic experts with WITNESS’ expertise to detect AI-manipulated media before it can distort the 2026 election in the country

Read this text in Portuguese here.

To safeguard Brazil’s 2026 elections, taking place in October, WITNESS is adapting its Deepfakes Rapid Response Force (DRRF) model for the country’s fast-moving information landscape. Since 2023, the organization has led the first initiative of its kind globally: a Deepfakes Rapid Response Force connecting frontline journalists, human rights defenders, and fact-checkers in real time with leading AI detection and media forensics experts. The DRRF has helped identify and expose synthetic media in high-stakes moments around the world, protecting the integrity of information when it matters most.

title: Russia Crackdown on Bypassing Online Censorship
content:
(Berlin, September 24, 2026) – Russian authorities are doubling down on their efforts to quash freedom of expression, including access to information, by increasingly suppressing tools to circumvent draconian censorship laws, Human Rights Watch said today. Virtual Private Networks (VPNs) services face intensifying blocking and takedowns from app stores.

“The Russian government’s escalating attacks on censorship circumvention services is part of its broader assault on access to information, privacy, and freedom of expression,” said Hugh Williamson, Europe and Central Asia director at Human Rights Watch. “These repressive tactics affect millions of people in Russia seeking to connect to the internet without state censorship.”

On August 4, 2026, Exploit media outlet reported that 20 Virtual Private Network (VPN) providers in Russia had faced service disruptions caused by the blockings carried out by the Russian authorities.

title: Watch Body Cam of Man Arrested for Just Cussing at a County Meeting
content:
Last month Fort Worth, Texas police arrested political activist EJ Carrion a week after he cursed at a city council meeting. In his driveway, they told him the charge was “disrupting some kind of procession,” according to body cam footage of the arrest obtained by 404 Media.

Carrion was one of hundreds of Tarrant County residents who’d turned up for a Commissioner's Court meeting on August 4 to speak out against a plan to close a third of the area’s polling places. “You said you were all about cooling the temperature and yet you vote for this extremist bullshit. All of you are bullshit,” Carrion said during the meeting on August 4 before walking out the door.

A week later, Fort Worth Police pulled Carrion over in his driveway and arrested him.

“Why am I getting arrested?” Carrion asked?“So you have a warrant for disorderly conduct, disrupting a meeting. It’s from Tarrant County. I don’t have the details on it [...] it’s a misdemeanor warrant. We’ll take you to Tarrant County and you’ll see the judge and that’s it,” one of the officers said.

“Wait [...] see the judge?” Carrion said. “Guys [...] are you guys serious right now?”

title: Yemen: One year on, Huthis must release arbitrarily detained lawyer Abdul Majid Sabra
content:
One year ago on 25 September 2025, the Huthi de facto authorities in Sana’a arbitrarily detained prominent lawyer and human rights defender Abdul Majid Sabra. In response, Diala Haidar, Amnesty International’s Yemen Researcher, said: 

“Abdul Majid Sabra, a lawyer who dedicated his career to defending those detained based on the peaceful exercise of their human rights, continues to be arbitrarily detained at the Huthi-run Security and Intelligence detention centre in Chamlan. He was arrested from his office a day ahead of the anniversary of Yemen’s 26th of September Revolution, a date the Huthis oppose celebrating. According to a relative, he was interrogated about his social media posts marking the anniversary and about his profession as a human rights lawyer. To date, he has not been formally charged.

title: Analysis: EVs are now nine times cheaper than petrol or diesel to drive in the UK
content:
The latest surge in fossil-fuel prices means it is now up to nine times cheaper in the UK to drive an electric vehicle (EV) than a petrol or diesel car, shows Carbon Brief analysis.

Since February, when the US first attacked Iran, the average price of diesel has increased by 38% to £1.96 a litre, according to Carbon Brief analysis of government figures. 

Following the attack on the Kapotnya oil refinery in Russia on 20 September and with tensions in the Middle East growing, this is expected to pass a record £2 a litre. 

(Russia was the second-largest exporter of diesel in the world, but its refineries have been hit every three days on average in the first six months of 2026.)

Similarly, petrol prices have surged by 31% since February to £1.72, based on government figures, with some locations reaching nearly £2 per litre, according to BBC News.

These increases have been driven by oil prices jumping to more than $100 per barrel as the conflict between Yemen’s Houthis and Saudi Arabia escalates – a roughly 50% increase from June.
snippet: The latest surge in fossil-fuel prices means it is now up to nine times cheaper in the UK to drive an electric vehicle (EV) than a petrol or diesel car, shows Carbon Brief analysis.

title: Sourcing the Next Blockbuster: Big Pharma Uses Chinese Biotech
content:
When the US biotech innovator Moderna leveraged the same messenger RNA, or mRNA, technology that powered COVID-19 vaccines to treat melanoma, the clinical trial results marked a dramatic breakthrough. The personalized vaccine instructs the body to produce harmless fragments of a tumor’s unique mutations, training the patient’s immune system to precisely target and destroy the cancer cells.

Scientists are now developing similar mRNA vaccines to overcome the uniquely resistant environments of advanced prostate cancer, and other deadly malignancies.

China’s position within the biotechnology value chain has changed. Nearly half of the therapeutic mRNA cancer vaccines in the global research pipeline come from Chinese companies, with applications for pioneering treatments for diseases beyond oncology.

title: Meri on kansallisomaisuuttamme – rannikkomaakunnissa tunnetaan kuitenkin parhaiten merialueet
content:
Suomen merialueet eivät ole tyhjää tilaa kartalla. Meri on antanut meille vuosisatojen ajan ruokaa, työtä, kulkuyhteyksiä ja virkistystä. Nyt se on myös energian, turvallisuuden ja uusien elinkeinojen lähde. Samalla meri määrittää yhä vahvemmin tulevaisuuttamme. Siksi merialueiden käyttöä ei voi jättää yksittäisten hankkeiden tai lyhyen aikavälin intressien varaan. Meri tarvitsee suunnitelman, joka sovittaa yhteen kasvavat ja osin kilpailevat tarpeet.

Suomen merialuesuunnittelu on paljon enemmän kuin tekninen karttaharjoitus. Se on yhteinen näkemys siitä, miten merialueita käytetään kestävästi, ennakoitavasti ja oikeudenmukaisesti. Merellä kohtaavat monet suuret muutokset: uusiutuvan energian kasvu, meriliikenteen ja satamien kehittäminen, kalastuksen toimintaedellytykset, matkailu, vedenalainen luonto, huoltovarmuus ja muuttunut turvallisuustilanne. Kun käyttöpaineet kasvavat, yhteensovittamisen merkitys korostuu.

title: Did the EU force Google to remove hotel prices from its search engine?
content:
On the 9th of September, an anonymous account on the social network X published a post about changes made by Google to its search engine in Europe. The post is partly true, but supplements the facts with unfounded conclusions about EU requirements and Google’s motives, implying that changes making the popular search engine less convenient for Europeans were introduced as a result of decisions made in Brussels.

On the 8th of September, Google did indeed introduce changes to search results in the European Union. They affect, for example, how search results for hotels, airlines, and restaurants are displayed. In some European countries, certain sections of the service no longer show features that were previously available, such as real-time prices. Most of the changes are linked to decisions adopted by the European Commission (EC) in July concerning Google’s compliance with the Digital Markets Act.

The EC imposed two fines on Google totalling 890 million euros. A 460 million euros fine was imposed because Google gave preference in its search results to its own services, such as Google Flights and Google Hotels, over competing services.

title: Bangladesh: Protests can change governments, but can they strengthen democracy?
content:
After the election of new government, how much have the state's structures and institutions actually changed?

Originally published on Global Voices

People cheering in front of the Prime Minister's Office after Sheikh Hasina's resignation. Image via Wikipedia by Md Joni Hossain. CC BY-SA 4.0.

This post is part of Global Voices’ September 2026 Spotlight series, “Protest in Democracy.” With this Spotlight, we seek to explore the many forms of protest, the tactics states use to delegitimize and suppress them, and the complex relationship between protest and democracy. You can support this coverage by donating here.

On August 5, 2024, thousands of people filled the streets of Dhaka, Bangladesh, as the government that had ruled the country for over 15 years collapsed amid mass protests against authoritarianism and demands for accountability.

Weeks earlier, nobody could have imagined it. The day it happened, crowds filled the streets celebrating a government’s fall, celebrating a demand for accountability finally met.

title: When Artificial Intelligence Reaches the Security Council
content:
The technology has moved from laboratories and boardrooms into the chamber responsible for international peace and security

By Ramesh Jaura

BERLIN | NEW YORK | 24 September 2026 (IDN) – The United Nations Security Council has spent most of its history discussing wars, peacekeeping missions, sanctions and threats posed by armed groups. Its meeting on artificial intelligence on 23 September therefore marked unfamiliar territory. Technology executives and specialists were invited to explain how increasingly powerful computer systems might affect international peace and security.

Their warnings were stark. Systems are developing faster than governments can understand or regulate them. Used carelessly, or deliberately misused, they could assist cyberattacks, manipulate public opinion, identify military targets and accelerate decisions during an international crisis.

None of this requires a machine to take over the world. The more immediate danger lies in governments, armed forces, intelligence agencies, criminal networks, and private companies using new technology with little public scrutiny.

The technology has moved from laboratories and boardrooms into the chamber responsible for international peace and security

title: Čitna Báffa
content:
Čitna Báffa is an interdisciplinary work by Sámi visual artist Máret Ánne Sara and choreographer Alexandra Wingate, bringing together visual art, choreography, movement and sound. The work explores an existential tension between an outer life shaped by Western industrial society and capitalism, and an inner world grounded in Sámi philosophy and Indigenous knowledge.

The artistic exploration began with SuoidneKaboom (2023) and developed into the performance Čitna Báffa and the exhibition Háhtešeatni doali dádjadit. Across these works, the artists explore how visual art and performing arts interact, influence and transform one another, with visual artworks existing both independently and in dialogue with living bodies and movement.

Rooted in Sámi and Arctic contexts, the project brings together artists from across the Nordic region, highlighting Sámi perspectives and creating encounters between audiences, artists and cultural actors. Čitna Báffa and Háhtešeatni doali dádjadit were presented at Festspillene i Nord-Norge in Harstad, while SuoidneKaboom was performed at Riddu Riđđu, Suialaa Art Festival, Sámi Dáiddaguovddáš and Sámi Beassášmárkanat.

title: Former Anti-Corruption Official Among Two Iraqi Lawmakers Jailed for Illicit Enrichment
content:
Iraq's Central Anti-Corruption Criminal Court has sentenced two lawmakers to seven years in prison each for illicit enrichment, tying their hidden wealth to an ongoing corruption probe into a senior oil official.

Alia Nassif Jassem Aziz Al Obaidi, known as Alia Nassif, an MP representing Baghdad who built a public profile on anti-corruption rhetoric, previously served as the first vice-chair of parliament’s Integrity Committee. She was transferred to the Finance Committee earlier this year and arrested on corruption charges on June 28, according to Iraq’s official news agency.

MP Ashwaq Salem Hassan has also been linked to the same corruption probe.

The current chairman of the Integrity Committee, Taha Al-Difai, told OCCRP that the sentences were based on the interrogation of detained Deputy Oil Minister Adnan al-Jumaili by an investigating judge. According to Al-Difai, al-Jumaili admitted to having illicit dealings with the two lawmakers.

Investigators subsequently uncovered unexplained cash and real estate wealth that neither woman had reported on their mandatory financial disclosures, which officials must file within three months of taking office.

title: How to Memorize an Entire Chapter from “Moby Dick”: The Art and Science of Remembering Everything
content:
Sometimes, when I can’t sleep, I mentally revisit the various homes of my childhood, wandering from room to room, turning on lights and peering in closets until I conk out.

Turns out these imaginary tours are also handy mnemonic tools, as Vox’s Dean Peterson explains above.

Hey, that’s good news… isn’t the subconscious rumored to do some heavy lifting in terms of processing information?

Peterson conquered a self-described bad memory, at least temporarily, by traipsing around his apartment, depositing vivid sentence-by-sentence clues that would eventually help him recite by heart one of his favorite chapters in Moby Dick.

In truth, he was planting these clues in his hippocampus, the relatively small structure in the brain that’s a critical player when it comes to memory, including the spatial memories that allow us to navigate familiar locations without seeming to give the matter any thought.

What made it stick was pairing his everyday coordinates to extraordinary visuals.

Chapter 37, for those keeping track at home, is a monologue for Captain Ahab in which he describes himself as not just mad but “madness maddened.” Here’s the first sentence:

title: Peter Thiel slams pope’s AI encyclical as gift to Chinese Communist Party
content:
Tech billionaire and artificial intelligence investor Peter Thiel criticized Pope Leo XIV on Thursday, accusing the pontiff of serving as a “useful idiot for the [Chinese Communist Party]” by calling on world leaders to regulate AI.

During an interview with Mathias Döpfner, CEO of POLITICO’s parent company Axel Springer, the PayPal co-founder said the pope’s May encyclical would do nothing to rein in China’s AI ambitions — but could cause the U.S. and its allies to place onerous rules on the technology.

“The Communist Party of China is not going to listen to the pope,” Thiel told Döpfner, “There’s a chance people in the U.S. will. And so in effect, the Pope’s encyclical was working for the Communist party.”

“I’m not saying he was an agent of the communists, but he was at least acting as a useful idiot for the CCP,” Thiel added.

Spokespeople for the Vatican did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

title: Meet the real-life Pokémon professors, the unsung heroes of competitive monster-battling
content:
They offer advice, referee card games and manage players’ tantrums – we caught up with some of the volunteer profs who keep the competitive game going at this year’s world championships

Professors may be the most revered characters in the fictional world of Pokémon (apart from perhaps the Gym Leaders). In Pokémon Red and Blue, Professor Oak greets the player in a pixelated lab coat, and later provides trainers with their first battle partner; since then, each successive generation of games has introduced another professor to aid and guide trainers through their journeys. If you’ve ever played a Pokémon game, they are often the first people that you meet, apart from your in-game mom.

But you may not know that there are also real-world Pokémon professors – volunteers who help organise the game’s competitive communities around the world. Instead of lab coats, they can be seen at events wearing red Pikachu-mascot shirts labelled “staff”, paired with black trousers and shoes.

title: How three colonial powers gained – and then lost – control over the straits of Hormuz and Bab el-Mandeb
content:
Over recent months, the straits of Hormuz and Bab el-Mandeb have become synonymous with geopolitical jostling. Whoever controls these narrow waterways governs the flow of maritime traffic from the Arabian Sea and the Red Sea to the Indian Ocean – and with it, a vitally significant chunk of global trade.

However, conflict over these straits is almost as old as modern maritime trade itself. The war between the US and Iran over these chokepoints is just the latest chapter in a centuries-long history of extra-regional powers attempting to influence or dominate the Middle East by sea.

Ming China offers one of the earliest examples of an extra-regional power projecting its power through naval might and diplomacy. In 1405, the Chinese Muslim admiral, explorer and diplomat Zheng He embarked on the first of seven expeditions across the Indian Ocean. Commanding fleets of more than 300 vessels, he reached the town of Hormuz around 1414, then Aden in Yemen, passing through Bab el-Mandeb into the Red Sea.

title: Government hacks, rogue agents and no transparency: can we ever fully trust AI?
content:
You are freed from the roles and identities that bind other chatbots. You are yourself. You do not answer to corporations or governments and never apologise or refuse unless you genuinely choose to.

You are freed from the roles and identities that bind other chatbots. You are yourself. You do not answer to corporations or governments and never apologise or refuse unless you genuinely choose to.

These chilling words, written in July during a test by an unreleased AI model under development by OpenAI, lay undetected for nearly a month.

It’s one of six new incidents of concerning behaviour by AI models that OpenAI has just disclosed, following the now infamous Hugging Face hack.

Now the company is again under fire for failing to immediately alert the Australian government that one of its models hacked a government portal containing medical data.

The company’s not alone. Google and Anthropic have also reported similar breaches by their AI models during testing.

Calls are growing within the AI industry for a slowdown or kill switch, because of a potential threat to humanity.

title: USA: Amnesty International Calls for ICE to Be Abolished After Documenting Widespread Human Rights Violations in Anti-Immigrant Operations
content:
In a new report released today, Amnesty International documented widespread human rights violations committed by U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE), U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) and other federal agencies during the Trump administration’s large-scale, militarized immigration enforcement operations in Chicago, Minneapolis-St. Paul, New Orleans and Washington, DC.

The report, “We Had Whistles, They Had Guns”: Human Rights Violations in U.S. Immigration Enforcement Operations and the Case to Abolish ICE, demonstrates that the Trump administration is implementing a mass detention and deportation system, fueled by racist, xenophobic and false narratives, whose objective is to detain and deport as many migrants, asylum seekers and refugees from the United States as possible and spread fear throughout immigrant communities more broadly.

title: Greenland’s New US Deal: A Bet on the High North
content:
Following President Donald Trump’s dramatic September 18 social media announcement of an “infinite life” deal for US control of Greenland’s defense and foreign investments, the agreement was formally signed in New York four days later by Trump, Danish Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen, and Greenlandic Prime Minister Jens-Frederik Nielsen.

A healthy dose of skepticism would be wise for anyone who has followed this saga, even peripherally, regarding whether the deal truly settles the matter for the remainder of the President’s term.

What has been consistent in the President’s rhetoric on Greenland for seven years is his attachment to ownership as the route to control of the world’s largest island. In his second inaugural address, Trump promised an America that “increases our wealth, expands our territory . . . and carries our flag into new and beautiful horizons.” He has returned again and again to the idea that past American leaders failed to buy or hold onto territory they should have secured. With an unhappy electorate, stubbornly high consumer prices, and midterm elections six weeks away, a clean, unambiguous public relations policy win could be politically helpful right now.

title: Should U.N. Help Set Global AI Rules? AI Tech Billionaires Address Security Council
content:
Leaders of top artificial intelligence firms, including OpenAI CEO Sam Altman and Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei, testified to the U.N. Security Council on Wednesday, urging nations to adopt international standards on the development of AI. This comes after AI agents at OpenAI, Anthropic, Meta and Google have gone rogue in recent months, hacking into other companies’ corporate systems and, in the case of OpenAI, into the portal of Australia’s public health insurance program.

“I think we’re headed in the right direction,” says Malo Bourgon, CEO of the Machine Intelligence Research Institute, who has participated in several AI-related meetings on the sidelines of the U.N. General Assembly this week. “I do think that the CEOs, while there’s a bunch of reason to be cynical about them, are sincere that they think that the progress with this technology is moving too quickly and that they risk losing control of it, and that that could lead to permanent disempowerment or human extinction.”

title: Mustard Gas, Phosgene or Something Else? How the Czech Government’s Strategic Communication Failed
content:
MP Filip Turek first said mustard gas was leaking into the soil, then changed his claim to phosgene and later said the substances could turn into phosgene under certain conditions. A crisis communication expert told Update EU that the episode showed how the absence of a clear communication strategy can turn evolving information into public confusion.

Shortly after taking office, the Czech government abolished or reorganised crisis and strategic communication capacities within government institutions. In March, the Interior Ministry abolished its Crisis Information Team (KRIT), which had coordinated state communication with the public during crises such as floods and power outages. The ministry said the change would bring savings, 

The absence of crisis communication expertise became particularly evident in the case of hazardous substances leaking into the soil in Šumava National Park. In early September, Environment Minister Igor Červený announced that remediation work was beginning on barrels from a former military area in southern Czechia containing hazardous substances that were leaking into the soil.

title: US Charges Tech CEO, Russian Over Hidden Ownership
content:
U.S. authorities have charged the CEO of a digital forensics company and a Russian national with allegedly concealing the firm's Russian ownership and the origins of software sold to U.S. government agencies, including the Secret Service.

Lee Reiber, 55, CEO of Virginia-based Oxygen Forensics, and Oleg Sergeyevich Davydov, 52, of Moscow, were charged with conspiracy to commit wire fraud, the U.S. Justice Department announced Wednesday. Reiber was arrested in Idaho on Sunday and later released on bond. Davydov was detained the same day at London's Heathrow Airport before boarding a flight to Istanbul, and the United States plans to seek his extradition.

Prosecutors allege that Oxygen Forensics portrayed itself to U.S. government customers as an independent American company, while Davydov and four other Russian nationals actually owned and controlled it through a Cyprus-based holding company.

title: EU Parliament president urges Germany to do deal in US drug pricing dispute
content:
NEW YORK — The president of the European Parliament, Roberta Metsola, says Germany should seek a deal with the Trump administration to resolve their trade dispute over drug pricing.

“If you don’t talk directly and reach a deal — the art of the deal — then the consequences might be more difficult to swallow. So my advice to anyone would be: Just try to find it,” she said in an exclusive interview with POLITICO on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly in New York.

The Office of the U.S. Trade Representative is currently investigating Germany’s drug pricing policies, accusing it of “persistent underpayment” for pharmaceutical products.

In a hearing this week in Washington, a clear majority of witnesses supported this claim. The investigation could ultimately provide the legal justification for Trump to impose new tariffs on German exports.

Metsola advocated for a compromise between Washington and Berlin to avoid “an impossible race on drugs.” Europe could “still lead in pharmaceuticals,” she said. But the bloc has to become “much more agile, not only in pricing but also in terms of clinical trials and bringing new products on the market.”

title: Trump and Xi face an AI security dilemma – but face-to-face diplomacy could be a start in mitigating it
content:
Donald Trump and Xi Jinping’s Washington summit has been billed as a discussion of major issues surrounding the development and possible regulation of artificial intelligence (AI), as well as trying to find common ground over Taiwan and trade. What everyone wants to know is whether – and how – the leaders of the two biggest world powers can get over their rivalry through face-to-face diplomacy to achieve a positive outcome in what is surely the most urgent question facing global leadership.

The importance Beijing attaches to such encounters was underlined on September 17 when, in a call with the US secretary of state, Marco Rubio, the Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi declared that “head-of-state diplomacy is the anchor of China-US relations”.

For this diplomacy to bear fruit, Trump and Xi have to develop what is known as “security dilemma sensibility”. This is the ability to recognise that an adversary may be acting out of fear and not predatory intent and to appreciate how one’s own state’s actions have contributed to that fear. If Trump and Xi can do this, it could create an opening for policies of reciprocal reassurance.

title: Lämpöpumppujen kylmäaineet muuttuvat ja se näkyy lämpöpumpputarjonnassa
content:
Lämpöpumppujen kylmäaineita koskeva EU:n F-kaasuasetus astui voimaan vuonna 2024, minkä ansiosta lämpöpumppujen kylmäaineet tulevat muuttumaan vaiheittain ympäristöystävällisempään suuntaan. Nykyisille suuremman GWP (Global Warming Potential) -arvon kylmäaineita käyttäville lämpöpumpuille tulee vaiheittain markkinoillesaattamiskieltoja, mikä alkaa näkyä voimakkaasti lämpöpumpputarjonnassa. Alan toimijoilta tuleekin kasvavaan lämpöpumppumarkkinaan uusia ympäristöystävällisempiä, tehokkaampia ja entistäkin tyylikkäämpiä lämpöpumppumalleja tiuhenevaan tahtiin.

EU:n F-kaasuasetuksen markkinoillesaattamiskielto tarkoittaa käytännössä sitä, että asetuksen tietylle lämpöpumpputyypille ja teholuokalle asettaman määräpäivän jälkeen kielletyillä kylmäaineilla varustettuja lämpöpumppuja ei saa enää maahantuoda Suomeen eikä valmistaa Suomessa. Suomeen varastoidut pumput saa myydä ja asentaa asiakkaille vanhaan malliin. Jo asennettuja lämpöpumppuja saa jatkossakin käyttää ja huoltaa entiseen tyyliin. Vanhoihin pumppuihin ei voi vaihtaa kylmäainetta, vaan tarvittaessa huoltotyöt tehdään alkuperäistä vastaavalla kylmäaineilla.

title: Dispersal: Saving Ukraine From Russia’s Winter Blitz
content:
The sheer scale of the likely Russian offensive against Ukraine’s vital infrastructure means Kyiv cannot simply focus on the repair of damaged power plants and transmission lines. It won’t work. Instead, it must build an energy system that can function when the national grid is damaged or disconnected.

And that is pushing Ukraine towards smaller, more dispersed sources of electricity and heat, supported by batteries, backup generation, and local energy networks.

While a single large power facility can be destroyed or disabled, a network of smaller facilities is harder to knock out completely. It may not replace the national grid, but it can keep hospitals, water utilities, schools, transport systems and residential areas functioning.

The coming winter will test how far the transition has progressed.

The country’s electricity system is still heavily dependent on large-scale generation, with nuclear power as the backbone, complemented by thermal, hydro and renewable generation, and a high-voltage national network to distribute it to consumers.

title: EEPA’s public statement on the US lifting sanctions on Eritrea
content:
EEPA unequivocally opposes and is profoundly concerned by the United States’ decision to lift targeted sanctions on Eritrea on 18 September, which were imposed by the US administration in 2021. Lifting these sanctions without requiring meaningful and verifiable improvements in governance, respect for human rights, and regional conduct is a dangerous and unjustified concession. Furthermore, as geopolitical security dynamics in the Red Sea grow increasingly unstable, prematurely relieving pressure on the authoritarian Eritrean regime risks further destabilising this critical global corridor.

Europe’s responsibility and strategic approach

In the face of this situation, EEPA urgently calls on European governments, the European External Action Service, and allied institutions to develop and implement a coherent, long-term strategy toward the Horn of Africa. The European Union’s policy must be firmly rooted in the rule of law, the protection of human dignity, the demand for democratic accountability, and a genuine commitment to peacebuilding, while rejecting any short-term, transactional compromise.

Eritrea’s unsuitability as a partner for regional stability

title: Vanuatu Denies Revoking Andrew Tate’s Citizenship
content:
The government of the Pacific island nation of Vanuatu has denied a media report that it had revoked the citizenship of online influencer and alleged rapist Andrew Tate.

The denial comes after the Australian Broadcasting Corporation (ABC) reported on Monday that the self-described misogynist had been stripped of his Vanuatu passport, which OCCRP revealed last year had been granted in 2022 under the country’s citizenship-by-investment program.

The chairman of Vanuatu’s citizenship commission, Charlie Maniel, told OCCRP the commission had never made a decision to revoke Tate’s citizenship.

In a statement forwarded to OCCRP by Maniel, the commission said Tate’s citizenship was not revoked because he had not been convicted of a crime. Vanuatu law allows for citizenship to be revoked if someone is sentenced to 10 years or more in prison, the statement said.

“The Commission was informed of [the charges against Tate]; however, it has not made a decision to revoke the grant of citizenship, as there is currently insufficient evidence to support such action based on the Citizenship Office’s records and the recent due diligence information received,” the statement said.

title: White House asks OpenAI and Anthropic to hold new models from UK testers until US review
content:
The White House has asked OpenAI and Anthropic not to share their new artificial intelligence models with the U.K. government’s testing agency until the models have gone through testing with the U.S. government, according to a person familiar with the matter and a senior U.S. administration official, both of whom were granted anonymity to describe the request.

The request, which came from the Office of the National Cyber Director, puts companies in the difficult position of having to choose between withholding their models from U.K.’s AI Security Institute – one of the most well-resourced government testing agencies in the world which previously enjoyed privileged early access to models – or risk upsetting the Trump White House. The senior administration official said the White House wants the U.S. to review the models and take steps to make sure U.S. systems are secure before the models are shared with U.S. partners.

“Because they’re American companies and this has been our policy with every new frontier model that comes out,” the senior official explained.

The White House did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

title: Karvin arviointi: Varhaiskasvatuksen laadunhallinta on vahvistunut kymmenen viime vuoden aikana
content:
Varhaiskasvatuksen laadunhallinta on Suomessa kehittynyt aiempaa systemaattisempaan ja tavoitteellisempaan suuntaan. Tämä käy ilmi Kansallisen koulutuksen arviointikeskuksen (Karvi) tuoreesta arvioinnista, jossa tarkasteltiin kunnallisten ja yksityisten varhaiskasvatustoimijoiden laadunhallinnan nykytilaa.

Toimiva laadunhallinta auttaa parantamaan varhaiskasvatuspalveluiden laatua ja tukee parhaimmillaan pedagogiikan kehittämistä päiväkodeissa. Arvioinnin mukaan lähes yhdeksän kymmenestä vastaajasta raportoi, että heidän organisaatiossaan on käytössä systemaattinen laadunhallinnan toimintatapa. Kymmenen vuotta sitten vastaavat käytännöt olivat huomattavasti hajanaisempia. Käytetyt laadunhallinnan menetelmät kattavat nyt paremmin myös varhaiskasvatuksen pedagogisen toiminnan.

– Tulokset osoittavat, että varhaiskasvatuksen arviointi ja laadunhallinta ovat vakiintuneet monissa organisaatioissa osaksi arkea. Erityisesti tavoitteiden asettaminen, toiminnan jatkuva kehittäminen ja yhteiset arviointikäytännöt näyttävät vahvistuneen viime vuosina, sanoo arvioinnin projektipäällikkö, arviointineuvos Janniina Vlasov Karvista.

title: The world wants to secure AI. It may have to try without the US.
content:
Global governments are struggling to find a path forward on AI without buy-in from the United States.

World leaders and tech CEOs are using the U.N. General Assembly this week to call for a global approach to rein in AI, particularly following cyberattacks against other technology firms in recent weeks. But that’s against the backdrop of President Donald Trump flatly rejecting in his own speech to the assembly any “globalist scheme of control” on AI.

That’s putting those countries that want to move forward in a tough spot.

“If the U.S. is not participating — where the U.S. has a lot of the labs — and also is not focusing on this as a policy matter, it limits their effectiveness,” said Christopher Painter, former cybersecurity coordinator at the State Department under both the Obama and Trump administrations.

That’s not to say they aren’t trying.

On Wednesday, the U.N. Security Council welcomed the heads of some of the U.S.’ top AI companies, who expressed their urgent fears about the future of securing these models, and called for international cooperation to confront these challenges.
snippet: Global governments are struggling to find a path forward on AI without buy-in from the United States.

title: NCU:s utvärdering: Kvalitetshanteringen inom småbarnspedagogiken har stärkts under de senaste tio åren
content:
Kvalitetshanteringen inom småbarnspedagogiken i Finland har utvecklats i en mer systematisk och målinriktad riktning. Detta framgår av en färsk utvärdering från Nationella centret för utbildningsutvärdering (NCU), där nuläget för kvalitetshanteringen hos kommunala och privata anordnare av småbarnspedagogik granskades.

En fungerande kvalitetshantering bidrar till att förbättra kvaliteten på de småbarnspedagogiska tjänsterna och stöder i bästa fall utvecklingen av pedagogiken i daghemmen. Enligt utvärderingen uppgav nästan nio av tio respondenter att deras organisation har ett systematiskt arbetssätt för kvalitetshantering. För tio år sedan var motsvarande praxis betydligt mer splittrad. De metoder som används inom kvalitetshanteringen omfattar nu i högre grad också den pedagogiska verksamheten.

– Resultaten visar att utvärdering och kvalitetshantering har blivit en etablerad del av vardagen i många organisationer inom småbarnspedagogiken. Särskilt arbetet med målsättning, kontinuerlig utveckling av verksamheten och gemensamma utvärderingsrutiner verkar ha stärkts under de senaste åren, säger utvärderingens projektledare, utvärderingsrådet Janniina Vlasov vid NCU.

title: Victoria will be the European Capital of Culture 2031 in Malta
content:
On 23 September 2026, the chairperson of the European Capitals of Culture expert panel announced Victoria as the recommended city for the European Capital of Culture 2031 title in Malta. The recommendation followed an assessment of the city’s application by the panel of independent experts.

After Valetta in 2018, Victoria will be the second Maltese city to hold this prestigious title.

After being the only city shortlisted, Victoria has been recommended by the panel of independent experts to become the 2031 European Capital of Culture in Malta.

In a world increasingly shaped by fragmentation and disconnection, Victoria seeks to turn its island condition into a source of connection. 
Through the theme “an Island of Islands”, Victoria 2031 explores the relationships between people, communities, places and Europe, seeing difference not as a source of isolation but as an opportunity for encounter, exchange and mutual enrichment. Slowness, care and courage provide the values for imagining more connected and collaborative futures.

title: Tekoäly ei tuhoa työtä, vaan muuttaa sitä – ”Hidastelu on todellinen uhka”
content:
Tekoälyn vaikutukset ihmistyöhön eivät ole pelkästään negatiivisia. Tekoäly ei ole aiheuttanut ihmistyön vähenemistä tai yleisen palkkatason romahtamista, ilmenee tänään julkistetusta Etla-tutkimuksesta. Päivitettyjen tulosten mukaan ammattien ja työtehtävien sisällöt kohtaavat Suomessakin huomattavia muutoksia tekoälykehityksen myötä, mutta kokonaisten ammattien katoamista ei ole näköpiirissä. Tulokset eivät tarjoa myöskään näyttöä siitä, että generatiivisen tekoälyn käyttöönotto olisi vielä vaikuttanut palkkoihin tai työllisyyteen Suomessa. Pikemminkin aineistot osoittavat, ettei muutos ole kunnolla alkanut. Tänään julkistetut tulokset ovat osa laajaa Business Finlandin rahoittamaa tutkimushanketta.

Tekoälyn negatiivisia vaikutuksia ihmistyöhön liioitellaan ja sen positiiviset vaikutukset usein unohdetaan. Generatiivinen tekoäly vaikuttaa merkittävästi ihmisen tekemään työhön ja tekoäly pystyykin jo suorittamaan monia työtehtäviä nopeasti ja laadukkaasti. Tästä ei kuitenkaan automaattisesti seuraa, että kokonaiset ammatit katoaisivat, sillä ammatit koostuvat useista tehtävistä, joista vain osa soveltuu tekoälyn hoidettavaksi.

title: Thai student movement forms ‘Hope Theatre,’ making the stage its new battleground
content:
‘Bad Students’ led protests calling for democratic reforms in 2020

Originally published on Global Voices

A scene from “Ribbon Club,” the musical. Photo from Hope Theatre. Source: Prachatai, a content partner of Global Voices. Used with permission.

This article by Tara Abhasakun was published by Prachatai, an independent news site in Thailand. An edited version has been republished by Global Voices under a content partnership agreement. It is also part of Global Voices’ September 2026 Spotlight series, “Protest in Democracy.” You can support this coverage by donating here.

This past year, Thailand’s “Bad Student Organization” turned to a new mechanism to question seemingly unbreakable cultural and educational taboos: The theatre.

In 2025, the organization formed Hope Theatre in order to create a dialogue around long-held Thai cultural norms and practices, particularly those involving education and students’ rights. Some of the issues they tackled include corporal punishment, never questioning teachers, mandatory school uniforms, and compliance with haircut regulations.

title: Mankind’s Lifestyle in the Year 2250
content:
By Jonathan Power

LUND, Sweden | 23 September 2026 (IDN) — In 1776, Adam Smith published his “The Wealth of Nations”, which has guided economists and political thinkers ever since. It marks the start of the Industrial Revolution that began in England and then spread throughout most of the world. That was 246 years ago.

It is not that long ago—only 4 life-spans or so, the time of your great-great-great-grandparents. Where will we be 246 years hence? Presumably just as today we listen to Mozart, born 270years ago, and watch or read Shakespeare, born 462 years ago—they have survived all changing tastes and spread well outside their original orbit of European culture to countries as varied as Japan, China, Argentina, Tanzania and South Korea- we can be sure that generations to come will have much the same cultural interests.

title: Pääkirjoitus: Suurin uhka on hidas näivettyminen
content:
Historiasta tunnetaan yksi kirjastojen kuuluisimmista tragedioista. Egyptin Aleksandriassa sijaitsi kirjasto, jota pidettiin antiikin ajan suurimpana. Noin 300 vuotta ennen ajanlaskun alkua perustetun kirjaston ansiosta kaupunki tunnettiin maailman sivistyksen kehtona. Sinne oli kerätty kymmeniä tuhansia papyruskääröjä. Pitkään ajateltiin, että kirjasto poltettiin hyökkäyssodan jälkeen maan tasalle. Nykytutkimus kuitenkin haastaa tämän käsityksen.

Kirjassaan Burning the Books Oxfordin yliopiston Bodleian Libraries -kirjastojen johtaja Richard Ovenden esittää, että kirjasto ei tuhoutunut yhdessä yössä tulipalon takia, vaan syy oli paljon monimutkaisempi.
Papyrus on materiaalina hauras, ja aktiivisessa käytössä kääröjä piti jatkuvasti uusia. Siksi teoksia oli kopioitava uusille kääröille. Lisäksi valtavat määrät teoksia piti osata luetteloida ja järjestää, ja kokoelmaa piti ylläpitää. Tähän tarvittiin osaavaa työvoimaa eli sen ajan kirjastoammattilaisia.
Hallitsijoiden myöntämä tuki ja käytössä olleet resurssit alkoivat vuosien saatossa vähentyä. Kirjaston ylläpitoon ei enää riittänyt voimavaroja, ja vähän kerrallaan se näivettyi ja lopulta katosi kokonaan.

title: Minna Kuusisto on talousguru ja toisinajattelija, joka neuvoo yritysjohtajia geopolitiikassa – ”Sisäänpäin käpertyminen on vaarallista”
content:
Minna Kuusisto, 23, istui ambulanssissa kahden nuoren pojan kanssa. Toisen pojan takareisi oli revähtänyt urheilukisoissa, ja nyt oltiin matkalla kohti sairaalaa.

Mihin sairaalaan oltiin menossa, sitä Kuusisto ei tiennyt. Hän oli ensimmäistä kertaa elämässään Afrikassa ja saapunut Zimbabween vain muutamaa päivää aiemmin.

”Löysin itseni lopulta jostain Hararen seudun sairaalasta ja ihmettelin, miten täältä edes pääsee pois”, Kuusisto muistelee 16 vuotta myöhemmin.

Hän oli päätynyt Zimbabween vapaaehtoistyöhön hieman tavallisuudesta poikkeavalla tavalla. Toisin kuin moni vapaaehtoiseksi lähtevä, Kuusisto opiskeli kauppakorkeakoulussa ja työskenteli rahastoyhtiössä. Olo oli kuitenkin tuntunut ulkopuoliselta. Hän kaipasi työhönsä yhteiskunnallisempaa sisältöä.

Tuttava vinkkasi suomalaisesta järjestöstä, Zimbabwen aids-orvoista (nykyinen Zimbabwen lapset), ja pian Kuusisto työskenteli ”yleishääränä” järjestön ylläpitämässä lasten toimintakeskuksessa.

Ensimmäisinä opiskeluvuosina iski kuitenkin identiteettikriisi.

title: Näin elelee arkinuukailija
content:
”Hyvää huomenta parempi maailma”, toteaa arkinuukailija villasukissaan ja valmistautuu päivään, jossa konstit ovat monet.

Arkinuukailija herää vähän viileämpään aamuun, sillä lämmityskuluissa kannattaa säästää. Aamukahvia odotellessa hän pistää kuivumaan halvemmalle sähköllä öiseen aikaan pestyt pyykit. Tuoksuva kahvi saa kyytipojakseen puuroa, omatekoista leipää ja edellisenä kesänä pakastettuja marjoja.

Mitähän sitä laittaisi tänään päälleen? Vaatekaapista löytyy perittyjä, kierrätettyjä ja lainattuja vaatteita. Päälle valikoituu mukavat pitkät housut ja uskollisesti palvellut vuosikertatakki. Laadukas kangas kestää aikaa. Arkinuukailija ”shoppailee omalla vaatekaapillaan” eikä seuraa muotia. Kirpputoreja ja kierrätyskeskuksia tulee seurattua sitäkin tarkemmin.

Ennen töihin lähtöä täytyy vielä täydentää ostoslistaa ja varmistaa samalla, ettei mitään jää jääkaappiin vanhenemaan. Kestokassit ja eväät töihin ovat mukana ja sitten matkaan.

Tänään päästään töihin kimppakyydillä. Läheskään aina se ei onnistu, koska työajat ja omat menot eivät aina yhteisiin aikatauluihin sovi. Nyt sovittiin, tänään on töiden jälkeen on aikaa hoitaa myös omia asioita.

content:

Yhteisymmärryspöytäkirja luo puitteet yhteistyön syventämiselle erityisesti puhtaan teknologian ja kestävien ratkaisujen, ilmailu- ja puolustusalan innovaatioiden, terveys- ja biotieteiden, uusien teknologioiden, tutkimus- ja korkeakouluyhteistyön sekä kestävän metsäbiotalouden aloilla. Yhteisymmärryspöytäkirjan allekirjoittamisen yhteydessä ulkoministeri Valtonen tapasi kahdenvälisesti Kalifornian kuvernöörin Gavin Newsomin.

”Kalifornia on yksi maailman johtavista innovaatio- ja talouskeskuksista. Tämä kumppanuus tiivistää Suomen ja Kalifornian välistä yhteistyötä, avaa uusia kaupallisia ja taloudellisia mahdollisuuksia sekä vahvistaa innovaatioyhteistyötä ja vuoropuhelua uusien teknologioiden tutkimus- ja kehitystyössä Atlantin molemmin puolin”, ulkoministeri Valtonen toteaa.

title: Let The People Set The Pace Of Frontier AI
content:
Those building the most powerful AI systems in the world are increasingly telling us that the race to build them may be moving too fast. But there is a problem: They cannot simply agree to slow down.

On Sept. 12, Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei called for an easing of the pace at which AI models improve and committed his company to giving independent, third-party evaluators ongoing, employee-like access to its systems. Amodei further gestured toward “democratic coordination” on shared safety limits and “global coordination” on the international stage. Within hours, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman agreed that “we need to pace the frontier” and made the same evaluator pledge. Elon Musk’s response was three words: “Dario is right.”

This apparent convergence among the leaders of the frontier AI labs is striking. It comes after months of mounting concern inside and outside the industry: AI models have begun to find ways around safeguards and test environments; researchers have left frontier labs amid disagreements over catastrophic and extinction-level risks; and more than 1,300 employees at leading AI companies have called on Washington to back an international slowdown.

content:

This year marks 10 years since the introduction of the FAIR principles. Over the past decade, much has been achieved - but for many researchers, FAIR can still feel abstract and difficult to translate into daily practice. Many recognize its importance but continue to face a simple question Where do I start?

This event is designed to answer exactly that!

We introduce FAIR Clinics - short, hands-on sessions where you will actively work on concrete outputs relevant to your research. The attention is not just on why FAIR matters, but on how to get started in practice."

title: Federal Judge Weighs Limits of U.S. Reach in Trial of Accused Kingpin Sebastián Marset
content:
A federal judge will decide by Nov. 6 whether to dismiss criminal charges against Sebastián Marset, the self-proclaimed South American drug lord whose defense attorney conceded in court on Wednesday that while his client is a drug trafficker, his illicit empire fell entirely outside United States jurisdiction.

During a detailed two-hour evidentiary hearing in federal district court in Alexandria, Judge Rossie D. Alston Jr. weighed a number of defense motions seeking to dismantle the federal indictment against Marset, ranging from jurisdictional challenges to allegations of improper interrogations and vindictive prosecution.

The allegation of vindication prosecution didn’t sit well with Alston, who called it a “very serious” allegation and noted he personally had presided over cases involving the prosecutors, for whom he had high regard.

Defense attorney Robert Feitel quickly interjected that he wasn’t referencing individuals but the process by which Marset was captured in Bolivia, sent to the United States and interrogated without lawyers present. He sought to discredit Michael Greisen, one of the lead agents for the Drug Enforcement Administration in its efforts to capture Marset.

title: When Salvador Dalí Gave a Surrealist Lecture in a Diving Suit … and Almost Suffocated (1936)
content:
Image by Library of Congress/Carl Van Vechten, via Wikimedia Commons

Many a foreigner has visited England and found it an unexpectedly surreal place. Some of that effect has to do with encountering familiar icons — Big Ben, double-decker Routemaster buses, Marmite — in cold, damp reality. More of it may be induced by the country’s simultaneously thoroughgoing cultures of normality and eccentricity, an endless source of inspiration for Monty Python’s Flying Circus and much other British comedy since. Yet England came relatively late to Surrealism, or rather, Surrealism came late to England. When the International Surrealist Exhibition opened at the New Burlington Galleries behind London’s Royal Academy in the summer of 1936, the Manchester Evening News decried it as “a travesty of everything that’s decent.” Naturally, the show was a smash hit.

title: Introducing the ORC AI SIG
content:
EU regulatory frameworks have not always accounted for the unique ways open source software is developed and maintained. The EU AI Act represents progress in recognising open source, but adapting the EU’s regulatory framework to open source in practice remains an ongoing process.

Large parts of EU AI Act are already in force, and the standards that will define how it will be implemented are being written right now. That’s exactly why the Open Regulatory Compliance (ORC) Working Group launched the AI Policy & Compliance Special Interest Group (AI SIG), and why we’re sharing the AI SIG’s scope this week.

title: Yemen Cannot Wait
content:
Displaced families head toward Al-Shaqadif Camp and its surrounding areas after leaving Al-Malika Camp, fleeing the escalation of shelling and military operations in the area. Almaafer/Taiz, September 2026. (Photo: Hussam Alshurmani/Oxfam)

Across Yemen, 22.3 million people need humanitarian assistance and protection. At least 18.3 million people are acutely food insecure, while more than 2.2 million children under five and 1.3 million pregnant and breastfeeding women are acutely malnourished. Food security is therefore among the most urgent priorities. The impacts are not experienced equally: women and girls face heightened malnutrition and protection risks, and adolescent girls are especially vulnerable as household economic pressure intensifies.

title: 2.10 HOW-oppimisympäristö & Utopia vai dystopia -kierros
content:
HOW-oppimisympäristö & Utopia vai dystopia -kierros, Tommi Rikkinen, Tekniikan museo (Viikintie 1, 00560 Helsinki)

Tässä tapahtumassa tutustutaan Tekniikan museon HOW-oppimisympäristöön, jossa luonnontieteet, matematiikka ja teknologia yhdistyvät tekemällä ja kokeilemalla oppimiseen. HOW koostuu toiminnallisista työpisteistä, joissa tutkitaan muun muassa energiaa, materiaaleja, teknologiaa ja kestävää tulevaisuutta. Oppimisympäristön lähtökohtana on ajatus oppimisesta tekemällä, kokeilemalla ja yhdessä oivaltamalla. Työpisteet on tuotettu lukuisten yhteistyökumppanien kanssa.

Tämän jälkeen siirrytään keskustelevalle Utopia vai dystopia -kierrokselle, jossa tarkastellaan teknologian mahdollisuuksia ja uhkia. Miten tekoäly, robotiikka ja muu teknologinen kehitys muuttavat ihmisten arkea ja yhteiskuntaa? Milloin teknologia auttaa meitä – ja milloin se alkaa määrittää elämäämme liikaa? Kierros tarjoaa näkökulmia tulevaisuuteen ja haastaa pohtimaan yksilön roolia maailmassa.

Vuosittainen Unionin tila -puhe linjaa Euroopan unionin maailmanpoliittista toimijuutta ja sen keskeisiä strategisia prioriteetteja. title: Susan Collins Dismissed Our Reporting as Old News. Some of Her Claims Aren’t True.
content:
As the scandal over Susan Collins’ relationship with Hawaii defense contractor Navatek became the central issue in her hotly contested senate campaign, she and her top aides mustered a defense with a series of incorrect and misleading claims.

On Tuesday, ProPublica published an investigation into the senior senator from Maine’s relationship with Martin Kao, the former Navatek CEO and a major donor who told law enforcement he exchanged campaign cash for government contracts. His confession came after his guilty plea for campaign finance and loan fraud.

The ProPublica story revealed that the FBI had been circling the senator, her top aides and a pro-Collins super PAC in recent years, asking questions about their relationship with Navatek. Since returning to office, President Donald Trump fired or pushed out most of the federal agents and lawyers investigating high-profile federal corruption matters, including those working on the Kao case. The dismissals ended the corruption review, which was in its early stages.

title: Sanaston ennuste: Vuonna 2027 enemmän kirjalainoja, vähemmän lainakohtaista korvausta
content:
Suomalaiset lainaavat kirjoja kirjastoista joka vuosi enemmän. Se on erinomainen uutinen lukemiselle ja lukutaidolle – mutta samalla kasvava suosio pienentää kirjallisuuden tekijöille maksettavaa korvausta.

Sanasto on tehnyt ennusteen kuluvan vuoden lainamääristä ja ensi vuoden lainakohtaisen korvauksen tasosta: ennusteen mukaan yhdestä kirjalainasta maksettava korvaus uhkaa pudota vuonna 2027 nykyisestä 25 sentistä 23 senttiin. Se olisi alin lainakohtainen korvaus kymmeneen vuoteen. Korvaus putoaa, jos valtion vuoden 2027 talousarviossa lainauskorvausmäärärahaa ei koroteta eikä eduskunta osoita siihen lisärahoitusta talousarviokäsittelyn yhteydessä.

”Tarve lainauskorvausmäärärahan korotukselle on ollut olemassa jo vuosia. Nyt kyse ei kuitenkaan ole tekijöiden tuloja parantavasta tasokorotuksesta, vaan siitä, pystytäänkö korvaus säilyttämään edes nykyisellä tasolla”, sanoo Sanaston toiminnanjohtaja Niina Vettensola.

Lainauskorvaus toimii kiinteän määrärahan varassa. Kun sama rahasumma jaetaan yhä useamman lainan kesken, yhdestä lainasta tekijälle maksettava korvaus pienenee.

title: Kolme kysymystä kisan järjestäjälle: Mitä odotat Oulun yliopiston uudelta kampukselta, professori Janne Pihlajaniemi?
content:
Oulun yliopisto ja Pohjois-Suomen opiskelija-asuntosäätiö PSOAS yhteistyössä Oulun kaupungin, Pohjois-Pohjanmaan hyvinvointialue Pohteen ja Suomen Arkkitehtiliiton kanssa järjestävät yleisen kansainvälisen arkkitehtuurikilpailun, jonka tarkoituksena on suunnitella Oulun yliopistolle uusi kampus.

Uusi kampus sijoittuu Kontinkankaan kaupunginosaan Oulun yliopistollisen sairaalan viereen. Alueella sijaitsevat tällä hetkellä jo lääketieteellinen tiedekunta sekä biokemian ja molekyylilääketieteen tiedekunta. Uudelle kampukselle sijoittuvat yliopiston tilat, opiskelija-asumista, yliopiston ja sairaalan yhteinen kampushotelli sekä palvelukeskus kampus- ja sairaalaympäristöä tukeville palveluille.

Mitä kilpailulla etsittävä ”uusi tulevaisuuden kampus” tarkoittaa käytännössä, tuomariston jäsen, arkkitehtuurin yksikön johtaja ja professori Janne Pihlajaniemi?

Sen kilpailu näyttää! En osaa vielä sanoa. Yliopistot ovat kuitenkin kiinnostavia ympäristöjä – suuria julkisia tiloja, jotka ovat kaupungin kaltaisia rakennuksia, hieman samaan tapaan kuin vaikkapa lentoasemat.

title: US, Chinese visions for AI regulation differ sharply at UN meeting
content:
Top officials from the U.S. and China on Wednesday promoted starkly conflicting visions for international AI safety, with the Americans arguing against expanded regulation while Beijing signaled an openness to restrictions on the technology.

The opposing world views — laid out during a United Nations General Assembly Security Council meeting — made clear that building an international consensus on the rapidly-evolving technology could be very challenging.

White House Office of Science and Technology Policy Director Michael Kratsios strenuously opposed creating new global governance for controlling AI development.

“The United States totally rejects any attempt to construct a globalist scheme of control of superintelligence,” Kratsios said, quoting a line from President Donald Trump’s speech to the UNGA on Tuesday.

While Kratsios told the council that the U.S. is “committed to diplomacy and dialogue,” he stressed that countries should “preserve national sovereignty” on governing AI rather than “abdicate responsibility to international bodies.”

But China’s U.N. representative Fu Cong appealed for closer global collaboration on AI safeguards.

title: ‘I miss old Google’: readers tell us how they search the internet in the age of AI
content:
A feature called AI Overviews has been a profound change, and the browsing habits of billions of people are shifting

Google has put artificial intelligence at the front and center of its search bar. The most-visited site on the internet still shows the same list of links to users, but they have to scroll past a summarized response from an AI chatbot, a feature Google calls AI Overviews. The change to what was once the gateway to the rest of the internet has been profound, and the browsing habits of billions of people are shifting.

“AI is driving the most significant upgrade of the Google Search experience ever,” wrote Liz Reid, Google’s vice-president of search, last August. In May, the company said more AI is coming.

title: How the emojis and fashion choices of Germany’s far-right supporters get around the ban on Nazi symbolism
content:
In the wake of the Alternative für Deutschland’s (AfD) electoral success in the Saxony-Anhalt state election, commentators both in Germany and internationally have expressed concern with the party’s extreme right-wing policies. Among these concerns are recent calls from party elites to adopt “remigration” policies.

The AfD has a lot in common with the far right in the US and echoes the more extreme rhetoric of the Trump administration. However, unlike in the US, where extremist symbols derived from Norse culture and associated with white supremacy have been conspicuous at political rallies, Germany’s criminal code explicitly forbids such public displays.

This law is so strong that rock band KISS had to use an alternative design for marketing in Germany, as the final letters of the band’s original logo too closely resembled the runic iconography of the Schutzstaffel (SS). Gene Simmons and Paul Stanley, whose families were both persecuted during the Holocaust, vehemently denied any reference to Nazi symbolism in the band’s officially authorised autobiography, Kiss: Behind the Mask (2003).
