title: The UN is facing a crisis of trust and possible bankruptcy. Its new leader will have an enormous challenge
content:
The United Nations is deep into the process of looking for its next Secretary General as Portugal’s Antonio Guterres steps down in December after a decade.

The leadership change comes as the 81-year-old organisation faces many serious challenges. Who will step in and tackle them with the skills and courage they demand remains an open question.

There is no legislated date for UN member countries to decide on the new Secretary General; it depends on when the Security Council agrees on its preferred candidate. Ultimately, the decision has to be made before December 31.

The campaign to take over from Guterres is unfolding against the background of a crisis of trust in the international system generally, and in the UN in particular.

International cooperation between some countries is in the process of unravelling. Many are turning away from international dialogue, despite cyclical conflict in hot spots in Africa and the Middle East continuing, and global threats like climate change, health pandemics and competition in newly contested areas like the Arctic, cyberspace, outer space and the oceans.

title: Carl Sandburg, Woody Guthrie, Pete Seeger, Lead Belly & One Legendary Banjo
content:
—This article also appears in the September/October issue of the Library of Congress Magazine.

It was 1939, and friends gathered in the bohemian heart of Greenwich Village to toast the publication of a new book by one of their own. Frank Warner, a musician and folksong collector, arrived with a prized new possession in hand: a handmade banjo, fresh from the mountains of North Carolina.

Nathan Hicks had crafted this fretless, five-string instrument from figured walnut just months earlier, and Warner quickly customized it to his own style, adding frets and removing the drone string.

That evening, amid the good cheer and easy laughter, Warner impulsively decided on another alteration. He turned to Carl Sandburg, the famed poet, song collector and Lincoln biographer, and held out the banjo. Would you mind signing it?

Sandburg obliged, scrawling his name and the year beneath the bottom string.

The banjo Nathan Hicks crafted in 1939, now with 260 signatures. American Folklife Center. Photo: Shawn Miller.

That, as it turned out, was just the start.

PL Ukazało się drugie, zaktualizowane wydanie publikacji Niematerialne dziedzictwo kulturowe. Zbiór dokumentów pod redakcją naukową Hanny Schreiber. Książka jest dostępna również bezpłatnie w wersji elektronicznej.

Pierwsze wydanie Zbioru ukazało się w 2023 roku, w 20. rocznicę przyjęcia Konwencji UNESCO w sprawie ochrony niematerialnego dziedzictwa kulturowego. Publikacja gromadzi najważniejsze dokumenty tworzące międzynarodowe i krajowe ramy ochrony niematerialnego dziedzictwa kulturowego, w tym materiały po raz pierwszy udostępnione w języku polskim.

Drugie wydanie zostało przygotowane w związku ze zmianami, jakie w ostatnich latach zaszły w tym obszarze. Obejmuje zaktualizowane wprowadzenie, aktualizację dokumentów, których treść uległa zmianie od czasu pierwszego wydania, a także polskie tłumaczenie nowego dokumentu UNESCO z 2025 roku dotyczącego ochrony niematerialnego dziedzictwa kulturowego w kontekstach miejskich (Guidance Note on safeguarding intangible cultural heritage in urban contexts).

is an interactive, browser-based visualisation of the carbon cycle at different stages of a Finnish forest's rotation period. It offers anyone interested in the topic an easy and illustrative way to explore how carbon moves through forests. Carbon Forest shows when forests act as carbon sinks, when they are carbon sources, and which kinds of forests make the best carbon stores.

Developed at the University of Helsinki, Carbon Forest is aimed at anyone who wants a basic understanding of how the carbon cycle works in Finnish forests. It is also suitable for use in science education. The service also provides concise, easy-to-understand descriptions of the most common forest characteristics from the perspectives of both the carbon cycle and biodiversity.

Carbon Forests' data are based on the SMEAR measurement network of the University of Helsinki's Institute for Atmospheric and Earth System Research (INAR), its long-term measurements and the scientific publications based on them. Carbon Forest is part of the online service.

title: Väitös: Työttömyys ja ilmastonmuutos ovat yhteydessä mielenterveysongelmiin
content:
Työttömyyden kasvu näkyy selvästi myös väestön mielenterveydessä, osoittaa Oulun yliopiston tuore tutkimus.

Taloustieteen väitöskirjatutkija Saqib Amin tarkasteli työttömyyden ja mielenterveyden yhteyttä Suomen kunnissa vuosina 2002–2019. Tutkimuksessa hyödynnettiin Tilastokeskuksen ja Terveyden ja hyvinvoinnin laitoksen rekisteriaineistoja, jotka kattoivat 98 prosenttia suomalaisista.

Kun paikallinen työttömyysaste nousi, myös masennuslääkkeiden käyttö ja psykiatrisen hoidon tarve lisääntyivät.

Erityisen voimakkaasti yhteys näkyi 25–64 -vuotiailla miehillä. Yhden prosenttiyksikön nousu työttömyysasteessa johti tässä ryhmässä psykiatristen osastohoitojaksojen kasvuun melkein 9 prosentilla. Masennuslääkkeitä käyttävien osuus kasvoi 0,28 prosenttiyksikköä.

"Perinteisissä suomalaisissa teollisuusyhteisöissä miehen identiteetti ja itsearvostus ovat edelleen vahvasti sidoksissa taloudelliseen tuottavuuteen ja elättäjän asemaan. Työpaikan äkillinen menetys ravisuttaa identiteettiä ja lisää alttiutta ahdistukselle, masennukselle ja vakaville psykiatrisille häiriöille", Amin sanoo Oulun yliopiston tiedotteessa.

title: Alexander Stubb YK:n yleiskokouksessa: yhteistyötä konfliktien sijaan
content:
Presidentti Alexander Stubb puhui YK:n yleiskokouksen yleiskeskustelussa New Yorkissa. Puhe pidettiin tiistaina YK:n korkean tason viikon yhteydessä. Stubb käsitteli puheessaan muun muassa kansainvälistä yhteistyötä, maailman konflikteja ja Suomen ehdokkuutta YK:n turvallisuusneuvoston jäseneksi vuosille 2029–2030.

Presidentti Alexander Stubb ilmoitti YK:n yleiskokouksessa, että Suomi hakee turvallisuusneuvoston jäseneksi vuosille 2029–2030. Puheessaan Stubb korosti yhteistyön merkitystä aikana, jolloin maailmassa on paljon konflikteja ja kansainvälisiin sääntöihin kohdistuu kasvavaa painetta. Hänen viestinsä oli selkeä: valtioiden välisen kilpailun sijaan tarvitaan enemmän yhteistyötä.

Stubb ehdotti myös YK turvallisuusneuvoston uudistamista. Hänen mukaansa Aasialle, Afrikalle ja Latinalaiselle Amerikalle pitäisi antaa lisää paikkoja, ja veto-oikeudesta tulisi luopua.

Lisäksi Stubb nosti esiin kolme keinoa maailman epäjärjestyksen vähentämiseksi: kansainvälisen oikeuden kunnioittamisen, humanitaaristen periaatteiden puolustamisen sekä rakentavan vuoropuhelun.

title: Central African Republic: ICC Verdict in Seleka Commander Case
content:
(The Hague) – The International Criminal Court (ICC)’s conviction of Mahamat Said Abdel Kani for crimes against humanity in the Central African Republic offers an important measure of long-awaited justice for victims of the abusive Seleka armed group, Human Rights Watch said today. 

In 2012, the predominantly Muslim Seleka rebels ousted the Central African Republic president, François Bozizé, and seized power through a campaign of violence and terror. In March 2013, the Seleka took control of Bangui, the capital, attacking civilians and pillaging the city. In late 2013, Christian and animist militias known as anti-balaka, began to organize counterattacks against the Seleka. Both the Seleka and anti-balaka have been implicated in widespread atrocities against civilians.

title: An Invisible Force Has a Mysterious Effect on Aging, Scientists Discover in 'Startling' Breakthrough
content:
Scientists have discovered that the removal of Earth's magnetic field influences the lifespans of fruit flies in complex ways, a finding that sheds light on the aging process as well as the risks of future human space travel, according to a study published in the journal Aging on Wednesday. 

All life on Earth has evolved under the planet’s geomagnetic field, a vast bubble lined with electrical currents that is generated in the core and extends out into space. This protective magnetic shield is a major factor in Earth’s habitability, as it wards off harmful radiation from space, allowing life to flourish on the surface. 

Many migratory animals—including fish, birds, and insects—can clearly sense Earth’s magnetism and use it for navigation. But much less is known about how the field interacts with living cells and their components, such as mitochondria, the famous “powerhouses” that generate most of the energy that fuels life.

title: Nepali Activist at U.N. Rally Calls for Climate Justice After Deadly Glacier Floods Kill Thousands
content: In the wake of devastating flash floods triggered by glacial collapse in the Himalayas, Nepal is demanding climate reparations from polluter countries as it embarks upon the grueling process of rebuilding. Over 1,400 bodies have been recovered from the disaster, with around 6,000 others still missing. Nepal’s government estimates that the cost of infrastructure reconstruction is likely to exceed $4 billion. Nepal contributes less than 0.1% of global carbon emissions, yet as a mountainous country surrounded by glaciers, continues to be vulnerable to the effects of climate change. Recent studies estimate that global surface temperatures will likely exceed 1.5°C above preindustrial levels by the end of the decade.

title: Tekoälymurros pikemminkin lisää kuin vähentää ihmistyötä
content:
Tekoäly muuttaa ihmisten työtehtäviä, organisaatiorakenteita ja liiketoimintamalleja, mutta se ei hävitä ihmistyötä eikä romahduta keskimääräistä ansiotasoa. Tekoäly korvaa osan nykyisistä tehtävistä, mutta se myös täydentää ihmisten työtä, parantaa tuottavuutta ja synnyttää kokonaan uusia tehtäviä. Näiden yhteisvaikutus ihmistyön määrään on todennäköisesti myönteinen.

Suomen työmarkkinat kattavan kuukausiaineiston tulokset eivät anna näyttöä siitä, että generatiivisen tekoälyn käyttöönotto olisi vielä vaikuttanut palkkoihin tai työllisyyteen. Työmarkkinoiden varsinainen tekoälymurros näyttää olevan vasta edessä. Haasteena on, että teknologian mahdollisuudet kehittyvät huomattavasti sopeutumiskykyämme nopeammin.

Suomen suurin tekoälyyn liittyvä riski ei ole massatyöttömyys vaan tekoälyn liian hidas käyttöönotto. Tekoälyn mahdollisuudet voidaan hyödyntää täysimääräisesti vain uudistamalla samalla työtapoja, organisaatiorakenteita ja liiketoimintamalleja.

title: Pskov’s medieval religious art is being appropriated by the Russian state to support the invasion of Ukraine
content:
Russian soldiers are appearing alongside saints in artwork at Russian Orthodox Churches

Originally published on Global Voices

Church of Saints Cosmas and Damian of Primostye.  Address: 7 Leona Pozemskogo Street, Pskov. Date: 2010. Source: Licensing: Ostrogolovy, from Russian Wikipedia, the copyright holder of this work, has voluntarily released it under the Creative Commons CC0 1.0.

The Russian authorities and the Russian Orthodox Church, which has expressed its full support for the Russian full-scale invasion of Ukraine and continues to do so, have appropriated the traditional Pskov style of Orthodox icons in support of the war in Ukraine.

In the spring of 2026, the Pskov Oblast governor wrote in his Telegram channel that two soldiers who died in combat during the Russian aggression in Ukraine have been depicted as icons, which are displayed in one of the famous Pskov churches.  

Both paratroopers shown on the icons were professional soldiers from Russia’s 76th Air Assault Division, based in Pskov. Both had taken part in the war against Ukraine from the first day and were killed there in 2023.

title: Motivation and concerns regarding the use of preprints among Brazilian health researchers: a survey | medRxiv
content: Abstract: This study aimed to evaluate the motivations and concerns related to preprint use among Brazilian health researchers. A mixed-methods online survey of all 1,596 holders of CNPq Research Productivity Grants in seven health fields was conducted in 2025. The questionnaire was adapted from a survey of bioRxiv authors, translated into Portuguese, and pilot-tested. Closed-ended responses were analyzed descriptively, and free-text responses were grouped by similarity. Overall, 178 researchers accessed the survey (11.2%), and 143 answered items on preprints and were included in the final analysis (9.0% effective response rate). The mean age was 55.9 years, and 88.0% were affiliated with public institutions. Regarding corresponding-author publications over the previous five years, 62.2% of respondents had deposited no preprints, while 37.8% had deposited at least one. Among preprints users, 79.2% agreed that deposition was freely decided by the authors. The main motivations were rapid sharing of findings (69.8%) and obtaining feedback (49.1%). title: Azerbaijan Pardons French Citizen as EU Lifts Sanctions on Russian Billionaire
content:
President Ilham Aliyev of Azerbaijan pardoned 20 prisoners on Wednesday, including a French national jailed on espionage charges, shortly after the European Union removed Russian-Uzbek billionaire Alisher Usmanov from its sanctions list.

Among those granted clemency under Aliyev’s decree was Martin Ryan, a French citizen arrested in late 2023 and sentenced by an Azerbaijani court in March to 10 years in prison.

The pardons followed a broader diplomatic deal struck after France lobbied for Usmanov's delisting. The E.U. Council announced Tuesday that it had also lifted sanctions against Mikhail Fridman, a Russia-connected businessman, while extending restrictions—including travel bans and asset freezes—on roughly 3,000 other individuals and entities for three years in response to the Kremlin’s war in Ukraine.

title: Watch Interplanetary Revolution (1924): The Most Bizarre Soviet Animated Propaganda Film You’ll Ever See
content:
In 1924, Zenon Komissarenko, Youry Merkulov and Nikolai Khodataev produced Interplanetary Revolution, which might just be one of the strangest Soviet propaganda films ever produced.

First, the film is animated using not only traditional cel animation but also collage and stop motion, giving the work a queasy, disorienting feel. A bit like looking at a painting by Henry Darger.

Then there is the film’s story. As an intertitle proclaims, this is “a tale about Comrade Coninternov, the Red Army Warrior who flew to Mars, and vanquished all the capitalists on the planet!!” This already sounds better than John Carter.

title: The Federal Agency That’s Supposed to Protect Consumers Just Made Another Business-Friendly Move
content:
Every year, millions of complaints flow to the federal Consumer Financial Protection Bureau from people across the country. The complaints, which range in focus from debt collection to credit reporting to payday loans and more, long served as a window into Americans’ gripes and struggles with various companies.

For over a decade, consumers could opt in to have what they wrote published as public information in a CFPB database. But last month, the Trump administration announced that it would stop publishing those complaint narratives, a decision that aligns the agency with corporations that have critiqued the system for years. 

“Publishing such narratives in the Database provides a less-than-representative sample of one-sided experiences,” the CFPB said in a press release.

In the big picture, the move is part of a trend of the administration taking a friendlier approach with businesses — even at the federal agency tasked with guarding consumers from unfair and deceptive practices.

title: Rakennusperintö-SAFAn blogi: Suomen Pankki – arkkitehtuurikilpailun ja rakennusperinnön kestävä jälki
content:
Vierailulla Suomen Pankin johtokunnan varapuheenjohtaja Marja Nykänen piti puheen talouden tilasta ja hallintopalvelutoimiston toimistopäällikkö Hannu Vesalainen esitteli rakennuksen historiaa.

Suomen Pankilla on kunnia ja velvollisuus pitää huolta kulttuuriperinnöstämme sekä toimintaympäristöstään muuttuvassa maailmassa. Suomen Pankki (1811) ja Suomen markka (1860) ovat vanhempia kuin Suomi itsenäisenä valtiona. Oma raha ja oma keskuspankki mahdollistivat osaltaan irtautumisen Venäjästä. Tänä päivänä yksi Suomen Pankin tehtävistä on ylläpitää rahoitusjärjestelmämme vakautta.

Suomen Pankin päärakennus ei kuitenkaan ole säilynyt muuttumattomana. Alun perin Ludwig Bohnstedtin voittaneen kilpailuehdotuksen pohjalta toteutettu rakennus on nykyään useiden arkkitehtien luovan työn tulos. Muun muassa F. A. Sjöström, Albert Mellin, Gustaf Nyström, Eliel Saarinen, Armas Lindgren, W. G. Palmqvist, Harry W. Schreck ja Arkkitehdit NRT ovat olleet vaikuttamassa siihen, millaisena Suomen Pankin päärakennus on säilynyt.

title: Why fans are digging their claws into Wolverine over its patronising gameplay
content:
From highlighted ledges to characters telling you what to do, blockbuster games are increasingly taking the challenge out of playing – and players are pushing back

• Don’t get Pushing Buttons delivered to your inbox? Sign up here

Marvel’s Wolverine, the latest action game from Sony’s stable of expensive blockbuster-factory studios, has had an unfortunate launch. Reviews were decent, if not stellar, but a series of viral video clips from reviewers and streamers have made it the scapegoat for a patronising flavour of game design that gamers have hated for decades. This clip, from Skill Up’s review, shows the player entering a beautiful wintry landscape before being overwhelmed by visual cues telling them what they’re supposed to be doing there. Sonar pulses point you in the direction of objectives. Targets – which, it bears emphasising, are shaped like targets – get an extra reflective visual effect so you know you’re supposed to pay attention to them. A trail shows you not just where to go, but where the level’s sole hidden collectible is.

title: Elections in Brazil: A subdued, digital campaign heightens uncertainty about the results
content:
With less than two weeks to go before voters head to the polls on Oct. 4, 2026, Brazil is experiencing a presidential election campaign that is much less heated than many would expect given the high-level of polarization in the country.

The latest polling also suggest few shifts in the political landscape, dominated by incumbent President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and his main right-wing challenger, Flávio Bolsonaro, the son of incarcerated former President Jair Bolsonaro.

But making predictions about Brazil’s presidential vote is a tricky business. In Brazil, voting is mandatory for literate citizens between 18 and 70 years of age, and if one presidential candidate doesn’t get to 50%+1 of the valid votes (not counting absentees and blank or invalid votes) in the first round, the field is narrowed to two candidates, who then face a run-off, scheduled for Oct. 25, 2026.

title: Saamelaisalueen koulutuskeskus vahvasti mukana arktisen alueen tulevaisuutta rakentavissa tutkimushankkeissa
content:
SAKK tuo NAFAS-, WITNESS- ja OADJEBAS-hankkeisiin alueellista, koulutuksellista ja saamelaiseen kulttuuriin liittyvää asiantuntemusta

Saamelaisalueen koulutuskeskus (SAKK) osallistuu kolmeen tutkimushankkeeseen: Antifragiilien arktisten järjestelmien rakentaminen Nexus-lähestymistavalla (NAFAS), WITNESS – kansalaisten toimijuus ja vaikuttaminen muuttuvalla arktisella alueella sekä Resilientin turvallisuuden tekeminen: Arktinen kansalaisyhteiskunta monikriisissä (OADJEBAS).

Hankkeet ovat saaneet rahoituksen Suomen Akatemian yhteydessä toimivalta strategisen tutkimuksen neuvostolta (STN). Hankkeissa etsitään ratkaisuja arktisen alueen nopeaan muutokseen, vahvistetaan paikallisten ja alkuperäiskansayhteisöjen toimijuutta sekä kehitetään turvallisuutta alueen omista lähtökohdista. SAKK on NAFAS-hankkeessa mukana konsortiopartnerina ja WITNESS-hankkeessa partnerina ja asiantuntijana. Lisäksi SAKK on mukana OADJEBAS-hankkeen käytännön toteutuksessa.

title: Canada: Press Vietnam’s Leader on Rights
content:
(Ottawa) – The Canadian government should raise the Vietnamese government’s poor human rights record during President To Lam’s visit to Canada on September 24, 2026, Human Rights Watch said today.

In a September 22 letter to Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney and Governor General Louise Arbour, Human Rights Watch expressed concerns that Vietnam’s agreements with Canada in recent years committing to human rights reforms have not resulted in improved respect for rights.

“The Vietnamese government’s intense crackdown on freedom of speech and association flies in the face of its human rights pledges to Canada,” said Patricia Gossman, senior Asia associate director at Human Rights Watch. “Canadian leaders should be clear that respect for human rights is crucial for strong diplomatic relations and trade deals.”

title: Woman Arrested, Dragged Away After Quietly Speaking About Flock at City Council Meeting
content:
Mia Hyder had never attended a public meeting before when she showed up to the city council meeting in Springfield, Missouri. After briefly speaking at a podium during a public comment period, she was arrested and dragged away in handcuffs. 

“Hello, my name is Mylie Hyder. I’m a Springfield, Missouri constituent, and I’m here to oppose the usage of ALPR cameras, most commonly made by Flock Safety. These cameras are not just surveillance,” Hyder started.

“I’m sorry ma’am,”  Springfield Mayor Jeff Schrag said. Her mic was cut. A cop approached her at the podium.

Hyder held up both of her middle fingers while continuing to speak: “They are an invasion of our privacy,” she said.

The cop said, “You’re under arrest,” grabbed her arms, and pulled her out of the room. “I can do this all night. I get paid by the hour,” the cop added.

“Does this conclude the public hearing,” Schrag said. 

“Yes sir,” a council member responded. The meeting continued with a city employee talking about sidewalk code. 

Hyder was one of two people arrested in Springfield, Missouri on Monday during a city council meeting where tensions rose after the council stalled a review of the city’s Flock cameras.

title: Suuntia suurille siirtymille: Oppeja Cartagena-tutkimushankkeesta
content: Teknologinen kehitys on keskeisin talouskasvun lähde, mutta sen vaikutukset tuottavuuteen ja hyvinvointiin riippuvat siitä, miten uutta teknologiaa otetaan käyttöön ja miten työ ja pääoma siirtyvät uusiin toimintoihin. Tämä muistio kokoaa yhteen Etlan toteuttaman ja Business Finlandin rahoittaman Cartagena-hankkeen tuloksia digitaalisesta ja puhtaasta siirtymästä sekä niitä tukevasta talouspolitiikasta. Tulosten perusteella tekoälyaltistus ei ole Suomessa toistaiseksi ollut systemaattisesti yhteydessä nuorten heikompaan työllisyys- tai palkkakehitykseen, eikä tekoälyn käyttö näytä heikentäneen työhyvinvointia. Henkilökohtaiseen kulutusdataan perustuva informaatio voi puolestaan muuttaa kuluttajien valintoja, joskin vaikutukset ovat keskimäärin maltillisia. Vihreän siirtymän vaikutus tuottavuuteen riippuu olennaisesti siitä, siirtyvätkö resurssit korkean vai matalan tuottavuuden puhtaisiin toimintoihin. Myös yritystukien vaikuttavuudessa keskeistä on niiden kyky synnyttää uusia investointeja, teknologian käyttöönottoa ja rakennemuutosta.

title: EPPO Arrests Suspect in $79M Cross-Border VAT Fraud Probe
content:
The European Public Prosecutor’s Office has arrested another suspect in its “Escape Room” investigation into a cross-border VAT carousel fraud network operating across six EU countries. 

The wider network allegedly used hundreds of shell companies and fictitious invoices to conceal transactions involving electronic devices and evade VAT in Austria, Belgium, Germany, Latvia, the Netherlands and Poland. EPPO estimates the scheme caused at least $79 million in losses in the Netherlands and Belgium. Eight other suspects were arrested in Belgium, the Netherlands and Poland in October 2025. 

Prosecutors allege the arrested man acted as a broker between companies in the scheme, improperly claimed VAT refunds and continued the operation through new companies after authorities raided the network in 2025. His activities alone may have caused about $4.6 million in losses, while authorities seized around $4 million in real estate, a car, stock, receivables and bank accounts.

title: Google’s content recommendation algorithm is a black box. Here’s how it decides what to show you
content:
If you’re one of Google Discover’s millions of daily users, you’ve doubtless come across all manner of content without actively searching for it. A Spanish user, for instance, might see headlines promising to reveal the secret recipes of avant-garde chef Ferràn Adrià, what time 46 year-old TV presenter Pilar Rubio goes to bed, the latest unmissable deals from Lidl, or the new car that will allow them to say “adiós” to annual inspections.

We still tend to think of Google as a search engine first and foremost. The iconic search bar on a white background – Alphabet’s flagship product that underpins its substantial advertising revenue – has long been part of our vocabulary, as both a noun and a verb that has the final say in contentious debates.

But over the years, Google has established another service, one that moves beyond traditional “searching” to algorithmic “finding”. Google Discover, its content recommendation system, has a similar interface to a social media feed, though without comments, retweets or visible interactions from other users.

title: Mosque attack highlights evolving extremism landscape that has brought Pakistan-Afghanistan ties to crisis point
content:
The suicide bombing and gun attack that killed dozens in northwest Pakistan on Sept. 18, 2026, highlighted the fragile security situation in the South Asian country. But it also shone a light on the complex and evolving extremism landscape there and the strained relationship between Pakistan and neighboring Afghanistan.

The assault took place as worshipers gathered for Friday prayers in the city of Kohat, in Khyber Puktunkhwa province, northwest Pakistan. A suicide bomber rammed an explosives-laden car through the wall of a police complex in the city of Kohat, targeting the mosque inside. Gunmen then exchanged fire with law enforcement officials during a 20-hour standoff. In all, 31 people were killed, including 16 police officers, while over 100 people were reported injured.

Supporters of the militant group Ittehad-ul-Mujahideen Pakistan, or IMP, claimed responsibility on encrypted apps like Telegram. But other seemingly aligned groups distanced themselves from the attack. Pakistan responded by conducting airstrikes in Afghanistan, home to at least one of the gunmen.

title: Trump’s Latest Media Attacks Again Hit Women Journalists
content:
Donald Trump’s tumultuous relationship with US journalists and legacy media reached a new crisis over the past week, as the US President banned three prominent outlets from accessing the White House or being part of the traveling press pool that accompanies the president to his engagements. He also promised further bans on other “Fake News Media Outlets.” Trump appears to have banned all staff from the three outlets—CNN, MS NOW, and Politico—from the White House. 

In practice, all three of the journalists who arrived at work on September 19, the day after Trump announced the ban, only to find that their entry was blocked, are women— Akayla Gardner from MS NOW, Cheyenne Haslett from Politico, and Betsy Klein from CNN. Ahead of his speech at the United Nations General Assembly this week, Trump singled out a fourth woman journalist, CNN’s Kaitlyn Collins, remarking, “You shouldn’t be here...you said you weren’t going to cover me.” Trump’s comment was likely a reference to CNN and other outlets’ decision to suspend pool coverage of the president after he banned CNN, Politico, and MS NOW from the White House.

title: Americans Fear AI Will Make the World Worse, Love It Anyway
content:
Most people in the world who use AI feel good about the technology and believe it will be a net positive for the future, according to a new study from Gallup. This is not the case in the United States, however, which is one of the few countries surveyed where negative emotions towards AI outweigh the positive. 

The new survey from Gallup and Microsoft polled people in 37 different countries about AI. “The study, which will ultimately cover 140 countries, measures public engagement with AI across five dimensions. In addition to emotional response, the survey captures awareness, frequency of use, expected impact and trust,” the study said.

Most people polled — a median of 81% — were aware AI tools exist, but only a median of 43% used them daily. Gallup told 404 Media it defined a “daily user” as an employed person who used AI everyday for either work or personal reasons or an unemployed person who used the tech every day.

title: "New Low in U.N. History": Trita Parsi on Trump's Threat to Annihilate Iran at General Assembly
content: The annual meeting of the United Nations General Assembly opened this week in New York City. On its opening day, President Trump in his address to all 193 U.N. member states threatened to annihilate Iran. “This is probably a new low in U.N. history,” says Trita Parsi of the Quincy Institute for Responsible Statecraft, joining us in our New York City studio ahead of the second day of the General Assembly. As Trump pushes for even more sanctions on Iran, “what you’re most likely to see in that scenario is that the Iranians will counter-escalate” in what threatens to become an “endless war.” Parsi also comments on the U.S. military’s growing reliance on artificial intelligence for strategic and targeting decisions, Trump’s upcoming meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping and the Trump administration’s flouting of international law.

title: Green, Yellow, Red: How Personalized Nutrition Feedback Shifts Grocery Purchases
content:
We studied whether personalized nutritional feedback on past grocery purchases shifts subsequent consumer choices. In September 2020, Finland’s largest grocery retailer added a Nutrition Calculator to its digital purchase-history service. The calculator summarizes the nutritional profile of customers’ purchases, evaluates it against national nutrition recommendations, and presents feedback using green, yellow, and red indicators. Using retailer transaction data, we estimate a difference-in-differences event study. Our primary specification compares 9,743 consumers who had used the service for at least six months before the launch of the calculator with a matched control group that had not activated the service.

The clearest effect is for sugar-intensive purchases, whose budget share falls by 0.25 percentage points on average and by up to 0.43 percentage points at the peak. The budget share of salt-intensive purchases also declines, although some of this movement predates the launch, making the evidence less conclusive. We found no systematic changes in the budget share of fat-intensive purchases. The effects are most pronounced among women and consumers under the age of 55.

title: Human Trafficking Raid Exposes Suspected Cyber Scam Operation in Papua New Guinea
content:
Papua New Guinea police rescued 39 Indonesians believed to have been trafficked to work in a cyber scam compound, the first case of its kind uncovered in the Pacific island nation.

Four Chinese nationals were also detained in connection with the Tuesday raid in the country’s capital, Port Moresby, PNG police Commissioner David Manning told OCCRP.

“What we did find in there was 39 Indonesian citizens, 34 that were male and five females, all adults but they’ve been in very cramped, very cramped conditions,” Manning said.

Manning also said police seized a large number of documents and electronic devices from the property, a house in Port Moresby’s inner suburbs. He said the incident was the first case he was aware of involving the suspected trafficking of foreign nationals into the country to carry out online fraud.

He added that as far as he is aware Papua New Guinea was the final destination for the suspected trafficking victims.

“All indications are they were brought in specifically to run this scam from Papua New Guinea,” he said.

title: Saddam Hussein used Oliver Reed and a James Bond director to tell Iraq’s story – but who tells it now?
content:
From the beginning of his brutal reign in Iraq, Saddam Hussein could claim an unusual credit: film producer. After Saddam became president in 1979, his cousin played him in The Long Days. The film dramatised his role in a failed 1959 attempt to assassinate Iraq’s then-prime minister, Abdul-Karim Qasim.

The film presented the new dictator as a hero. A few minutes in, a young Saddam calmly removes a bullet from his leg using a razor blade sterilised with fire. In his 2000 biography of Saddam, journalist Saïd Aburish called the story “an exaggeration of serious proportions”. He cited Saddam’s doctor, who said he had treated him only for superficial injuries.

In the same book, Aburish – who had been a consultant to Iraq’s Ministry of Information at that time – recalled how Saddam went through him to hire Terence Young to edit the production. Young had previously directed the James Bond films Dr No and From Russia with Love.

title: What you need to know about the EU’s new digital deportation regime
content:
On 17 June, the European Parliament approved the new deportation law (called the “Return” Regulation) which aims to track undocumented people down and deport them from the EU in large numbers. The Regulation boosts the surveillance powers and digital control of national authorities and will rely heavily on technologies and data collection in their enforcement. This blog outlines the various digital tools and processes included in the EU’s new digital deportation regime.

title: Former Mother-In-Law of Dismissed Ukraine Prosecutor General Denies Buying Dubai Villa
content:
With a cloud of controversy hanging over former Ukrainian Prosecutor General Ruslan Kravchenko — who was dismissed last week after his office was raided by anti-corruption officers — information has now emerged about a mystery villa in Dubai.

Records show Kravchenko’s former mother in law was listed as the owner of the Dubai villa. But she denies making the purchase.

Alina Shkrobanets acquired villa for about $670,000 in 2023, according to leaked Dubai property data obtained by OCCRP and shared with Schemes, the investigative unit of RFE/RL’s Ukrainian Service.

At the time, Kravchenko headed the Kyiv Regional Military Administration and was married to Alina Shkrobanets' daughter, Olena.

“I didn’t buy anything in the United Arab Emirates,” Alina Shkrobanets told Schemes, suggesting her identity details might have been used without her knowledge.

“I’m wondering if someone might have used my information against me,” she said in a phone interview.

title: ‘We Hacked the FBI:’ Hackers Say They Have Data on All FBI Employees
content:
A high profile hacking group claims it has breached multiple FBI-related services and stolen data “on all FBI employees and applicants.” A representative of the group, called ShinyHunters, told 404 Media the data includes FBI agents’ names, home addresses, phone number, and information on their spouse.

The data breach could be massively significant and may have all sorts of national security and counterintelligence implications. Criminals from the same ecosystem as ShinyHunters have previously used hacked data like phone records to track, intimidate, and harass the FBI agents investigating them. The highly sensitive data could also be a boon to foreign intelligence agencies who want to better understand how one of the most important law enforcement and intelligence agencies in the U.S. operates. And if the data fell into the hands of more criminals, FBI agents and their spouses could face serious threats to their safety.

“We hacked the FBI. We hold data on all FBI employees and applicants,” the representative of the group told 404 Media.

title: Ecuador: Militarization Continues and the Armed Forces Still Refuse to Cooperate
content:
One year after the publication of the report “It was the military. I Saw Them“, which documented the enforced disappearance of 10 people from the Ecuadorian coast, including six children, in the context of President Daniel Noboa’s so-called “Plan Fenix”, some progress has been made. Nevertheless, the lack of cooperation by the Armed Forces in the criminal investigations and the deepening of the policy of militarization of the public security continue to be the main obstacles preventing all victims’ families from obtaining truth, justice, and reparation, and from ensuring the non-repetition of these crimes, Amnesty International said today. 

“The progress achieved over the past year demonstrates that it is possible to respond to the demands for truth and justice made by the families, civil society, and international mechanisms. Yet this progress remains insufficient as long as many of those families continue not knowing what happened to their loved ones and the military authorities continue to withhold essential information for the investigations,” said Ana Piquer, Regional Director for the Americas of Amnesty International.

title: Explainer: How sea level rise poses an ‘existential threat’ to humans, heritage and nature
content:
For millions of people around the world, rising sea levels are already reshaping economies, livelihoods and cultures.

The world’s oceans are currently rising at a faster rate than at any time in at least the past three millennia, with human influence the “dominant cause” of sea level rise since at least 1970.

At the UN general assembly in New York this week, world leaders are set to adopt a high-level declaration on the “existential threats” posed by sea level rise. 

The declaration notes: “Sea level rise is not a distant scenario, but a real and lived experience for many.”

On average, global sea levels rose by 20 centimetres (cm) between 1901 and 2018. 

This is due to both the melting of glaciers and ice sheets and the expansion of seawater as it warms, as well as changes in land-water storage.

The rate of the rise has accelerated in recent years, with ocean levels rising 10.6cm since 1993. 

Sea level rise can vary locally due to seismic and volcanic activity, groundwater extraction and changes to the Earth’s surface resulting from ice melt.

title: Narrative Failure: Russia and the West have a Storytelling Problem
content:
Audiences respond to stories that drive toward an achievable climax. In the big movie of this summer, Odysseus faces endless challenges on his way home to Ithaca, but we know his goal is to reunite with Penelope and Telemachus and that he is handy with a bow. The story proceeds in an arc to his ultimate triumph.

Both Russia and the West have tried to promote a logical arc for the end of the Ukraine war, but their narratives have lacked goals and means. Both sides have failed to define exactly what they want, or to convince the world they have the ability to achieve it.

After Russia’s full-scale invasion, Western nations promised to give Ukraine “whatever it takes” without ever defining “it.” President Joe Biden’s administration never fixed a goal of entirely rolling back the invasion, nor did its European allies.

Three months after the invasion, Biden even implied Russia might keep some of its early territorial gains. He said the US would help Ukraine fight “further” aggression so it would “be in the strongest possible position at the negotiating table.”

title: "Pedagogy of the Oppressed" Brazilian Educator Paulo Freire Profiled in Film, "Reading the World"
content:
Reading the World is a remarkable new documentary about Paulo Freire, the acclaimed Brazilian educator whose revolutionary approach to teaching connected literacy to critical thinking and democratic participation. It draws on rare archival footage of 1960s Brazil and weaves together the memories of farmers, students and educators who took part in Freire’s culture circles, his method of teaching adults to read in as little as 40 hours by drawing on their own lives, communities and experiences. At the time, Brazil’s illiterate population was barred from voting, so education also opened the door to political participation. The experiment was abruptly halted in 1964 when Brazil’s military overthrew President João Goulart in a U.S.-backed coup that led to Freire’s imprisonment and exile.

“Paulo Freire was one of the most influential educators of the past century and is still widely studied all around the world. But the studies often focus on his ideas, his philosophies, his books, and much less is known about his original praxis,” says co-director Catherine Murphy.

title: ESG-tiedonantovaatimukset murroksessa 27.10.2026
content:
ESG-tiedonantovaatimukset murroksessa – mitä sääntely edellyttää sijoittajan, rahoittajan ja pörssiyhtiön näkökulmista?

EU:n kestävyysraportoinnin ja -tiedonannon sääntely elää poikkeuksellisen nopeaa muutosvaihetta. Omnibus I on jo voimassa, tarkistettuja ESRS-standardeja voi alkaa pian soveltaa, ja SFDR-uudistus etenee lainsäädäntöprosessissa. Muutokset eivät vähennä kestävyystyön merkitystä, mutta ne muuttavat sitä, kuka raportoi mitäkin ja kenelle.
Tule aamiaistilaisuuteemme kuulemaan, mitä Omnibus I:n soveltamisalan muutokset, tarkistetut ESRS-standardit ja SFDR-uudistus tarkoittavat käytännössä.

Ohjelmassa on ajankohtaiskatsauksen ohella paneelikeskustelu, jossa keskitytään ESG-tietoihin liittyviin kysymyksiin liiketoiminnan kannalta. Aihetta käsitellään kolmesta eri näkökulmasta: rahoittajan, joka tarvitsee kestävyystietoja rahoitettavilta yrityksiltä; sijoittajan, joka sekä pyytää dataa portfolioyhtiöiltään että kehittää yhtiöidensä vastuullisuustyötä; sekä pörssiyhtiön, joka raportoi suoraan CSRD:n nojalla ja vastaa samalla sekä sijoittajiensa että rahoittajiensa tietopyyntöihin.

Panelisteina:

  • Elina Erkkilä, ESG Director, OP Pohjola

title: Canada-EU alliance could be “beacon” for other democracies, Carney says. Australia is interested, Kyiv worries
content:
European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen’s State of the Union address stirred debate around the idea of a new form of closer association between Canada and the EU. Just a day later, Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney also took the floor in parliament. 

He clearly welcomed the idea of his country becoming a closer partner of the Union. He noted that a large majority of Canadians also support closer ties with Brussels and outlined how he envisages the functioning of the “new alliance”.  

“We are not fair-weather allies. We do not pursue zero-sum deals. Our commitment to the rule of law and our unyielding defence of human dignity, individual freedom and democracy share the same deep roots,” he said during his Thursday speech in Strasbourg. 

Carney noted that the world is currently being shaken by new challenges, from climate shocks and the undermining of democratic institutions to the weaponisation of the economy and various unfair practices by technology platforms.

title: Miten työ pidetään ihmisen kokoisena tekoälymurroksessa?
content:
Elovalkeat kokosi viime viikolla Tampereelle oppimisen ja osaamisen kehittämisen ammattilaisia pohtimaan, miten tekoäly muuttaa työtä, osaamista ja asiantuntijuutta. Keskustelu jatkui tällä viikolla eOppimiskeskuksen jäsenkahveilla.

Keskustelussa nousivat esiin erityisesti inhimillisyys tekoälymurroksessa, muuttuvat työtehtävät ja taidot, oppiminen arjessa sekä muutoksen konkretisointi. Miten työ pidetään ihmisen kokoisena? Miten osaamista kehitetään, kun tehtävät muuttuvat? Entä miten tekoälymurros tehdään ymmärrettäväksi yksilötasolla?

Kokonaiset ammatit eivät välttämättä katoa, mutta niihin sisältyvät tehtävät muuttuvat. Siksi oman osaamisen kehittämisessä kannattaa tarkastella ammattinimikkeiden sijaan sitä, mitä tehtäviä tekee, mitä taitoja työssä tarvitaan ja mikä osa omasta osaamisesta on siirrettävissä uusiin tilanteisiin.

Samat teemat ja kysymykset ovat myös Learning Factoryn toiminnan ytimessä: miten osaamista, työtä ja organisaatioita uudistetaan muuttuvassa työelämässä? Tutustu Learning Factoryn koulutuksiin, valmennuksiin ja sparrauksiin.

title: Inclusive European Heritage Residency 2026 in Malta: peer learning in practice
content:
From 13 to 19 September, Malta’s rich cultural heritage took centre stage during the second Inclusive European Heritage Residency, bringing together 10 selected participants from across Europe for peer learning activities and exchanges with dozens of volunteers and professionals from Din l-Art Helwa – the National Trust for Malta, as well as professionals from Europa Nostra and INTO.

The Residency aimed to strengthen the capacity and connections of heritage organisations across Europe, supporting more inclusive, sustainable and community-led approaches to heritage protection. The Residency was organised in the framework of the network project Europa Nostra Heritage Agora, co-funded by the Creative Europe Programme of the European Union.

title: Policy Area Education joins discussion at the EU Week of Regions and Cities on supporting young people
content:
Policy Area Education Coordinator, Anders Bergström from Norden Association Sweden, will contribute as a speaker to a workshop on supporting vulnerable young people as they move from adolescence into adulthood during the European Week of Regions and Cities in Brussels on 14 October 2026.

The workshop, “No child left behind: building bridges to adulthood”, will examine what happens when young people move beyond child-focused services and encounter fragmented systems across education, employment, housing, health and social support.

Participants will discuss how local and regional actors can create more integrated and youth-friendly pathways through coordinated support, early guidance, tailored referrals and stronger cooperation across sectors and levels of governance. The discussion takes place in the context of the EU Anti-Poverty Strategy and the strengthened European Child Guarantee.

The workshop is part of the European Week of Regions and Cities, taking place in Brussels in October. EUSBSR is participating in several activities during the week, including its own discussions on macro-regional cooperation.

Read more about the workshop and register on the event page.

title: From north to south, protests sweep across Tunisia: Is change at hand?
content:
Protesters are demanding development, jobs and dignity, the same slogans that drove the 2011 revolution

Originally published on Global Voices

Screenshot from video ‘Tunisians protest against the president: Critical infrastructure struggling to cope in summer’ on the Al Jazeera English channel on YouTube. Fair use.

This article, by Basma Barakat, was originally published in The New Arab on September 18, 2026. This edited version is republished on Global Voices as part of a content partnership agreement. It is also part of Global Voices’ September 2026 Spotlight series, “Protest in Democracy.” You can support this coverage by donating here.

Several Tunisian provinces are witnessing growing popular protests demanding development, jobs and dignity, the same slogans that drove the revolution that erupted on January 14, 2011.

For the first time since then, the general public are joining unemployed people in protesting, frustrated after years of unfulfilled promises, unenforced laws and deteriorating conditions.

title: TPS ja Ihmisoikeusliitto: Ihmisoikeudet kuuluvat urheilun ytimeen
content:
Lauantaina 3.10. pelattavan TPS–JYP-ottelun yhteydessä nostetaan esiin Ihmisoikeusliiton Älä riko urheilua -kampanjaa.

Turussa pelataan lauantaina 3.10. TPS:n ja Ihmisoikeusliiton yhteinen teemaottelu, kun TPS kohtaa Gatorade Centerissä JYPin. Yhdenvertaisuusottelussa nostetaan esiin Ihmisoikeusliiton Älä riko urheilua -työtä ja sen ydinviestiä: Ihmisoikeudet kuuluvat urheilun ytimeen. TPS ja Ihmisoikeusliitto haluavat yhdessä olla rakentamassa urheilumaailmaa, jossa jokainen voi urheilla turvallisesti ja omana itsenään. Kampanjan viestit näkyvät laajasti ottelutapahtumassa. TPS pelaa ottelun erikoispaidoissa, ja paitojen tuotot ohjataan Ihmisoikeusliiton Älä riko urheilua -työhön.

Ihmisoikeudet eivät vielä toteudu urheilussa kaikille. Haasteita on niin rakenteissa, toimintatavoissa kuin arjen tilanteissakin, eikä jääkiekko ole tästä poikkeus. Älä riko urheilua -kampanjan sanoin: Urheilu on rikki, jos lapsen oikeuksia ei turvata, jos rasismiin ei puututa järjestelmällisesti, jos sukupuolten tasa-arvo ei toteudu, jos seksuaali- ja sukupuolivähemmistöt eivät voi urheilla omana itsenään tai jos vammaisilla ihmisillä ei ole yhdenvertaista mahdollisuutta urheilla.

title: Why investigative teams fall into conflict — and what to do about it
content:
A room full of investigative journalists closed their eyes, took a sheet of A4 paper and followed a set of instructions. Fold it in half. Tear off the upper right corner. Fold it again. Tear off the lower right corner. No questions were allowed.

When they opened their eyes and unfolded the paper, the results were markedly different. Some had intricate patterns. Others were little more than shredded paper.

For Emma Thomasson, who was leading a workshop on communication and conflict at IJ4EU’s UNCOVERED Conference in Budapest, the exercise illustrated a basic problem in collaborative work: giving people the same instructions does not mean they will understand them in the same way.

“The point here is that communication is difficult, and particularly difficult if we are not all from the same background,” said Thomasson, a former Reuters bureau chief who now offers training and consulting on leadership, communication, innovation and workplace wellbeing.
